Title (English): Babylon, third world power
Description (English): Nebuchadnezzar became world ruler when he destroyed Jerusalem in 607 B.C.E.; his dynasty, the “head of gold” of Daniel 2, lasted until Babylon fell to the Medes and Persians in 539 B.C.E.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 607-ல் எருசலேமையும் அதன் ஆலயத்தையும் அழிக்க யெகோவா தேவன் அவரை அனுமதித்தபோது அவர் உலக ஆட்சியாளரானார் எனலாம்.
Main source: The Rise and Fall of an Immense Image

Title (English): Gedaliah appointed governor of Judah
Description (English): Nebuchadnezzar appoints Gedaliah son of Ahikam as governor over the Jews left in the land, a remaining vestige of Jewish self-rule.
Main source: Gedaliah

Title (English): Babylonians breach Jerusalem's wall
Description (English): After an 18-month siege, Nebuchadnezzar's army made a breach in Jerusalem's wall on Tammuz 9, in Zedekiah's 11th year.
Main source: Jerusalem

Title (English): Gedaliah murdered
Title (Tamil): “ஏழாம் மாதத்திலே” கெதலியாவும், இன்னும் சிலரும் கொலை செய்யப்பட்டனர்
Description (English): In the seventh month Gedaliah and others with him are assassinated, removing the last vestige of Jewish sovereignty in the land.
Description (Tamil): “ஏழாம் மாதத்திலே” கெதலியாவும், இன்னும் சிலரும் கொலை செய்யப்பட்டனர், ஆகவே மீந்திருந்த யூதர்கள் பயந்து எகிப்துக்கு ஓடிவிட்டனர்.
Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time

Title (English): Jews abandon Judah; 70-year desolation begins
Description (English): The remaining Jews flee to Egypt; from about October 1, 607 B.C.E., the land lies completely desolate, beginning the 70 years foretold by Jeremiah (ending 537 B.C.E.).
Description (Tamil): ஏறக்குறைய பொ.ச.மு. அக்டோபர் 1, 607-⁠லிருந்தே அந்தத் தேசம் முழுமையான கருத்தில் ‘பாழாய்க்கிடந்[து] . . . எழுபதுவருஷம் முடியுமட்டும் ஓய்ந்திருந்தது.’
Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
Where sources differ: date as given by merged duplicate b4-0003 (b4): Gedaliah assassinated; Jews abandon Judah; 70 years of desolation begin
Start/end of span: start of The 70 years of Judah’s desolation (b12-0024)

Title (English): The 70 years of Judah’s desolation
Description (English): After Gedaliah’s murder the remaining Jews fled to Egypt and the land lay desolate for the 70 years foretold by Jeremiah, until the exiles returned in the autumn of 537 B.C.E.
Description (Tamil): அவ்வாறெனில், பொ.ச.மு. 537-ம் ஆண்டின் இலையுதிர்காலத்தில் முடிவடைந்த இந்த ‘எழுபது வருஷங்கள்,’ பொ.ச.மு. 607-ன் இலையுதிர் காலத்தில் தொடங்கியிருக்க வேண்டும்.
Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time

Title (English): “Appointed times of the nations” begin to count
Description (English): With Judah abandoned in the seventh month, the “appointed times of the nations” begin to count.
Description (Tamil): ஏழாவது மாதம், யூதர்கள் யூதாவைவிட்டு வெளியேறுகிறார்கள்; “புறஜாதியாரின் காலம்” தொடங்குகிறது
Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
Start/end of span: start of “Seven times”: the appointed times of the nations (Gentile Times) (b12-0025)

Title (English): “Seven times”: the appointed times of the nations (Gentile Times)
Description (English): The “seven times” of Daniel 4, which Jesus called “the appointed times of the nations,” began when Babylon overthrew Jerusalem and the line of Davidic kings in 607 B.C.E. and ended in 1914 with the establishment of the Messianic Kingdom.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 607 அக்டோபரில், பாபிலோனியரால் எருசலேம் வீழ்த்தப்பட்டு, தாவீதின் வம்சாவளியில் வந்த ராஜா சிங்காசனத்திலிருந்து நீக்கப்பட்டபோது அந்த 2,520 வருட காலப்பகுதி ஆரம்பமானது.
Main source: Identifying True Worshipers in the Time of the End

Title (English): Prophetic activity of Obadiah
Description (English): Obadiah, a prophet of the seventh century B.C.E. about whom nothing personal is known, denounces Edom at the time of Jerusalem’s destruction.
Main source: A6-B Chart: Prophets and Kings of Judah and of Israel (Part 2)
Notes: Only an approximate single date is given. The A6 chart shows this prophet as an undated bar; range years come from the cited text sources. title_ta is the prophet’s name as printed in the Tamil A6 list.

Title (English): Ezekiel told that Jerusalem has been struck down
Description (English): In Babylon, an escapee from Jerusalem reached Ezekiel and reported that the city had been struck down; Ezekiel was then free to speak again to the exiles.
Description (Tamil): (33:17) இப்போது பொ.ச.மு. 607-ன் பத்தாவது மாதத்தின் ஐந்தாம் தேதி.
Main source: Bible Book Number 26—Ezekiel

Title (English): Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the immense image
Description (English): In the second year of his reign as world ruler (counted from Jerusalem's destruction), Nebuchadnezzar had a terrifying dream of an immense image; Daniel revealed and interpreted it.
Description (Tamil): நேபுகாத்நேச்சார் உலகை ஆட்சிபுரிந்த இரண்டாம் வருடத்தில் (பொ.ச.மு. 606/605) கடவுள் தந்த கனவால் அரண்டுபோனார்.
Main source: The Rise and Fall of an Immense Image

Title (English): Ezekiel's vision of a great temple
Description (English): In the 14th year after Jerusalem's destruction, the priest-prophet Ezekiel was transported in vision to a high mountain and beheld a great temple of Jehovah.
Main source: Temple

Title (English): Ezekiel foretells Egypt given to Nebuchadnezzar
Description (English): Ezekiel received a message that Egypt would be given to Nebuchadnezzar as wages for his campaign against Tyre; he inserted this later revelation into his book.
Description (Tamil): இங்கே, பொ.ச.மு. 591-ல் தனக்கு வெளிப்படுத்தப்பட்ட சில தகவல்களை எசேக்கியேல் இடையில் சேர்க்கிறார்.
Main source: Bible Book Number 26—Ezekiel

Title (English): Writing of Ezekiel completed
Description (English): The writing of Ezekiel was completed c. 591 B.C.E. Writer: Ezekiel; place written: Babylon. Time covered: 613–c. 591 B.C.E.
Description (Tamil): எசேக்கியேல்: எழுதியவர்(கள்): எசேக்கியேல்; எழுதப்பட்ட இடம்: பாபிலோன்; முடிக்கப்பட்ட வருஷம் (கி.மு.): ஏ. 591; காலப்பகுதி (கி.மு.): 613–ஏ. 591.
Main source: Table of the Books of the Bible
Notes: Writer(s): Ezekiel. Place written: Babylon. Writing completed: c. 591 B.C.E. Time covered: 613–c. 591 B.C.E.

Title (English): Nebuchadnezzar campaigns against Egypt (37th year)
Description (English): A fragmentary Babylonian text dated to Nebuchadnezzar's 37th year mentions a campaign against Egypt, possibly when Egypt was brought under Babylonian control as Ezekiel foretold.
Main source: Nebuchadnezzar

Title (English): Death of Nebuchadnezzar II
Description (English): After a 43-year reign (624-582 B.C.E.) that included his 'seven times' of madness, Nebuchadnezzar died in October 582 B.C.E.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 582-ல் கர்வம்பிடித்த நேபுகாத்நேச்சாரின் உயிர்பிரிந்தது.
Main source: Babylon
Chart hint: Covered by span – hide on chart
Start/end of span: end of Reign of Nebuchadnezzar II, king of Babylon (b12-0020)

Title (English): Evil-merodach succeeds Nebuchadnezzar
Description (English): Evil-merodach (Awil-Marduk) became king of Babylon after Nebuchadnezzar.
Main source: Evil-merodach
Where sources differ: Insight 'Babylon' says Nebuchadnezzar died October 582 and was succeeded by Awil-Marduk; Insight 'Evil-merodach' gives 581 for the succession (likely accession vs. first regnal year).

Title (English): Jehoiachin released from prison by Evil-merodach
Description (English): In the 37th year of his exile, Jehoiachin was released from the house of detention by Evil-merodach and given a position of favor above the other captive kings.
Main source: Jehoiachin
Where sources differ: Insight 'Evil-merodach' says the release was 'in the year of his becoming king' (581); Insight 'Jehoiachin' says 'evidently in 580 B.C.E.'
Start/end of span: end of Jehoiachin’s captivity in Babylon (b12-0021)

Title (English): Writing of 1 Kings completed
Description (English): The writing of 1 Kings was completed in 580 B.C.E. Writer: Jeremiah; place written: Judah. Time covered: c. 1040-911 B.C.E.
Description (Tamil): 1 ராஜாக்கள்: எழுதியவர்(கள்): எரேமியா; எழுதப்பட்ட இடம்: யூதா; முடிக்கப்பட்ட வருஷம் (கி.மு.): 580; காலப்பகுதி (கி.மு.): ஏ. 1040-911.

Title (English): Writing of Jeremiah completed
Description (English): The writing of Jeremiah was completed in 580 B.C.E. Writer: Jeremiah; place written: Judah; Egypt. Time covered: 647-580 B.C.E.
Description (Tamil): எரேமியா: எழுதியவர்(கள்): எரேமியா; எழுதப்பட்ட இடம்: யூதா; எகிப்து; முடிக்கப்பட்ட வருஷம் (கி.மு.): 580; காலப்பகுதி (கி.மு.): 647-580.
Main source: Table of the Books of the Bible
Notes: Writer(s): Jeremiah. Place written: Judah; Egypt. Writing completed: 580 B.C.E. Time covered: 647-580 B.C.E.

Title (English): Cyrus begins his reign
Description (English): Cyrus succeeded his father Cambyses I to the throne of Anshan in Persia about 560/559 B.C.E.; Diodorus places the start of his reign in Olympiad 55, year 1.
Description (Tamil): சுமார் பொ.ச.மு. 560/559-ல் கோரேசு புகழின் பாதையில் காலடியெடுத்து வைத்தார்.
Main source: Cyrus
Chart hint: Covered by span – hide on chart
Start/end of span: start of Reign of Cyrus the Great (b12-0026)

Title (English): Reign of Cyrus the Great
Description (English): Cyrus, the Persian conqueror of Babylon, reigned from 560/559 B.C.E. and issued the decree that let the Jews return home; he died on a military campaign in 530 B.C.E.
Main source: Cyrus

Title (English): Nabonidus begins to rule Babylon
Description (English): On the basis of cuneiform texts, Nabonidus is believed to have ruled Babylon some 17 years, from 556 to 539 B.C.E.
Description (Tamil): நபோனிடஸ் தன் ஆட்சியை பொ.ச.மு. 556-ல் தொடங்கியதாக நம்பப்படுவதால் அவருடைய ஆட்சியின் மூன்றாம் வருஷமும் ‘பெல்ஷாத்சாரின் முதலாம் வருஷமும்’ பொ.ச.மு. 553 ஆக இருந்ததென தெரிகிறது.
Main source: Nabonidus

Title (English): First year of Belshazzar: Daniel's dream of four beasts
Description (English): Belshazzar exercised royal authority from Nabonidus' third year on, evidently 553 B.C.E. In 'the first year of Belshazzar' Daniel had a dream and visions of four beasts, beginning the private visions of Daniel chapters 7 to 12.
Description (Tamil): இவருடைய ஆட்சி பொ.ச.மு. 553-ல் தொடங்கியிருக்க வேண்டும்.
Main source: Bible Book Number 27—Daniel
Notes: Daniel 8 vision ('third year of Belshazzar') has no B.C.E. date stated on jw.org sources checked; not included.

Date (as printed): About the middle of the sixth century B.C.E.
Title (English): Babylonian king Nabonidus conquers Edom
Description (English): Babylon’s peace with Edom did not last: about the middle of the sixth century B.C.E., troops of the Babylonian king Nabonidus conquered Edom. Insight and “All Scripture Is Inspired” present this as a fulfillment of the prophecies of Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and Obadiah against Edom (Obadiah 7: those ‘in covenant with’ Edom would prevail against her).
Description (Tamil): பாபிலோன் ஏதோமுடன் செய்த சமாதானம் நீண்ட காலம் நிலைக்கவில்லை. பொ.ச.மு. ஆறாம் நூற்றாண்டில், அரசன் நபோனிடஸின் பாபிலோனிய சேனைகள் ஏதோமை கைப்பற்றின.
Main source: Edom
Notes: No exact year is printed. Insight: “about the middle of the sixth century B.C.E.”; si (Tamil and English): “during the sixth century B.C.E.” Year 550 and sort_key -550 only place the event mid-century (Nabonidus began to rule in 556 B.C.E., b4-0019); do not display as a year.

Title (English): Cyrus conquers Media
Description (English): Cyrus gained a swift victory over Median King Astyages and captured his capital, Ecbatana, ending Median dominance over the Persians.
Description (Tamil): ஆனால் பொ.ச.மு. 550-ல் பெர்சிய ராஜாவான கோரேசு மேதிய ராஜாவான ஆஸ்டைஜிஸை எளிதில் தோற்கடித்தார்.
Main source: Persia, Persians

Title (English): Cyrus defeats Babylonian forces at Opis
Description (English): According to the Nabonidus Chronicle, in the month Tishri of Nabonidus' final year Cyrus attacked and defeated the Babylonian forces at Opis.
Main source: Cyrus

Title (English): Belshazzar's feast: Daniel interprets the handwriting on the wall
Title (Tamil): மேதியரும் பெர்சியரும் பாபிலோனைக் கைப்பற்றுகின்றனர்  மேதிய-பெர்சியா நான்காவது உலக வல்லரசாகிறது
Description (English): During Belshazzar's feast, a hand wrote on the palace wall; Daniel made known its meaning, that the kingdom was given to the Medes and the Persians.
Description (Tamil): 4 இந்த இரவில் அதாவது பொ.ச.மு. 539, அக்டோபர் 5/6-ன் இரவில் பாபிலோனியர்கள் இந்தளவு குடித்துக் கும்மாளமடித்தது வியப்பளிக்கிறது.
Main source: Babylon
Notes: [title_ta from owner's Tamil sheet]

Title (English): Babylon falls to the Medes and Persians
Title (Tamil): மேதியரும் பெர்சியரும் பாபிலோனைக் கைப்பற்றுகின்றனர்; மேதிய-பெர்சியா நான்காவது உலக வல்லரசாகிறது
Description (English): Cyrus' army entered Babylon without a battle during the night of October 5, 539 B.C.E. (Tishri 16); Belshazzar was killed, and Medo-Persia became the fourth world power of Bible history.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 539, அக்டோபர் 5/6-ன் இரவில், மேதிய-பெர்சிய படை, வெல்லமுடியாததாய் தோன்றிய பாபிலோனை வீழ்த்தி பெல்ஷாத்சார் ராஜாவை கொன்றபோது தானியேல் அங்கிருந்தார்.
Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time

Title (English): Medo-Persia, fourth world power
Description (English): Medo-Persia, the silver part of the image, replaced Babylon in 539 B.C.E. and ended when Alexander the Great defeated Darius III at Gaugamela in 331 B.C.E.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 539-ல் உலக மகா வல்லரசாக திகழ்ந்த பாபிலோனின் இடத்தைப் பிடித்தது மேதிய-பெர்சியா.
Main source: The Rise and Fall of an Immense Image

Title (English): Cyrus enters Babylon
Description (English): Seventeen days after the city fell, Cyrus himself entered Babylon on Marchesvan 3, according to the Nabonidus Chronicle.
Main source: Cyrus

Title (English): First year of Darius the Mede: Daniel receives the 70 weeks prophecy
Description (English): In the first year of Darius the Mede, Daniel discerned from Jeremiah's writings that the 70 years of desolation were nearing their end; he prayed and received through Gabriel the prophecy of the 70 weeks.
Main source: Two Kings in Conflict

Title (English): Cyrus issues decree freeing the Jews
Description (English): In his first year as ruler of Babylon, Cyrus issued a decree permitting the exiled Jews to return to Jerusalem and rebuild Jehovah's house; it was likely issued late in 538 or early in 537 B.C.E.
Description (Tamil): கோரேசு ஆட்சி துவங்கிய முதலாம் வருடம், பொ.ச.மு. 537-ன் வசந்தகாலத்திற்கு முன், யூதருக்கு விடுதலையளித்து கட்டளை பிறப்பித்தார்.
Main source: Cyrus
Where sources differ: Insight 'Jerusalem' dates the decree's going forth to Cyrus' first year (538 B.C.E.). | dp ch. 4 says 'In 537 B.C.E., Cyrus issued a decree'; Insight 'Captivity' says 'Early in 537 B.C.E.'

Title (English): Jews return to Jerusalem; 70-year desolation ends
Title (Tamil): எருசலேமுக்குத் திரும்பிச் செல்லும்படி அனுமதித்த பெர்சியனாகிய கோரேசின் கட்டளை செயல்படுத்தப்படுகிறது; எருசலேமின் 70 ஆண்டு பாழ்க்கடிப்பு முடிகிறது

Title (English): Antiochus II and Ptolemy II make an 'equitable arrangement'
Description (English): The king of the north, Antiochus II, and the king of the south, Ptolemy II, made an alliance; Antiochus divorced Laodice and married Ptolemy's daughter Berenice.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 250-ல் இந்த இரு ராஜாக்களும் ‘ஒருவரோடொருவர் சம்பந்தம் பண்ணிக்கொண்டார்கள்.’
People: Antiochus II; Ptolemy II Philadelphus; Berenice; Laodice
Main source: Two Kings in Conflict

Title (English): Death of Antiochus II
Description (English): When Antiochus II died, Berenice did not 'retain the power of her arm.'
Description (Tamil): அவர் பொ.ச.மு. 246-ல் இறந்தபோது, பெர்னைஸிக்கு தன் கணவரோடு இருந்த ‘புயபலம் இராமற்போயிற்று.’
Main source: Two Kings in Conflict

Title (English): Seleucus II retreats to Antioch
Description (English): With only a small remnant of his army, Seleucus II 'went back to his own soil,' retreating to the Syrian capital, Antioch.
Main source: Two Kings in Conflict

Title (English): Antiochus III marches against Ptolemy IV
Description (English): In the spring of 217 B.C.E., Antiochus III left Ptolemais and went north 'all the way to his fortress' in Syria after his clash with the king of the south.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 217-ன் இளவேனிற்காலத்தில், மூன்றாம் ஆண்டியோகஸ், தாலமேயஸ் நகரை விட்டு வடக்கே சென்று, சிரியாவிலுள்ள தன் ‘அரண்மட்டும் யுத்தங்கலந்து சேர்ந்தான்.’
Main source: Two Kings in Conflict

Title (English): Antiochus III takes Sidon and Jerusalem; Judea passes to the Seleucids
Description (English): After defeating Egypt's General Scopas at Paneas and taking Sidon, Antiochus the Great captured Jerusalem; Judea passed from the Ptolemaic king of the south to the Seleucid king of the north.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 198-ல், எருசலேமும் யூதாவும் எகிப்திய தென்றிசை ராஜாவிடமிருந்து சிரியா தேசத்து வடதிசை ராஜாவிடம் கைமாறின.
Main source: Jerusalem

Title (English): Macedonia and Greece fall to the Romans
Description (English): Macedonia and Greece, one of the four divisions of Alexander's empire, fell to the Romans.
Main source: Greece, Greeks

Title (English): Antiochus III's daughter marries Ptolemy V
Description (English): At the marriage of Antiochus III's daughter Cleopatra I to Ptolemy V, the Syrian king did not hand over the promised provinces.
Description (Tamil): இருந்தாலும் பொ.ச.மு. 193-ல் திருமணம் நடந்தபோது, சிரியா தேசத்து ராஜா இந்த மாகாணங்களை ஐந்தாம் தாலமிக்கு தரவில்லை.
People: Antiochus III; Ptolemy V; Cleopatra I
Main source: Two Kings in Conflict

Title (English): War in Greece draws in Antiochus III
Description (English): A war broke out in Greece, and Antiochus III was induced to come there, bringing him into conflict with Rome.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 192-ல் கிரீஸில் ஒரு யுத்தம் மூண்டது, இதனால் மூன்றாம் ஆண்டியோகஸ் கிரீஸுக்கு வர தூண்டப்பட்டார்.
Main source: Two Kings in Conflict

Title (English): Antiochus III defeated by Rome at Magnesia
Description (English): After losing the battle of Magnesia, Antiochus III had to give up everything in Greece, Asia Minor, and west of the Taurus Mountains.
Main source: Two Kings in Conflict

Title (English): Death of Antiochus III
Description (English): Antiochus III died while trying to rob a temple at Elymais, Persia.
Main source: Two Kings in Conflict

Title (English): High priest Onias deposed by Antiochus Epiphanes
Description (English): Antiochus IV Epiphanes deposed the Jewish high priest Onias; some Jewish commentators wrongly applied Daniel 9:26 to him.
Main source: Seventy Weeks

Title (English): Antiochus IV humiliated by Rome; Macedonia defeated
Description (English): Antiochus IV complied with Roman demands to withdraw from Egypt and returned to Syria; the same year Rome again defeated Macedonia.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 168-ல் அவர் சிரியாவுக்குத் திரும்புகிறார்.
Main source: The Two Kings Change Identities

Title (English): Antiochus IV desecrates the temple
Description (English): Seeking to Hellenize the Jews, Antiochus IV Epiphanes dedicated Jerusalem's temple to Zeus, built an altar on the great altar, and sacrificed swine there. This led to the Maccabean (Hasmonaean) revolt.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 167 டிசம்பரில், ஆலய பிரகாரத்தில் புறமத கடவுளுக்கு பலிபீடம் அமைக்கப்பட்டது.
Main source: Festival of Dedication
Where sources differ: dp ch. 13 dates the pagan altar to December 167 B.C.E.; Insight 'Festival of Dedication', 'Jerusalem', 'Greece' and 'Temple' give 168 B.C.E. (Chislev 25). Insight value used as primary.
Notes: display_ta/description_ta are from dp Tamil, which uses 167 (see conflicts).

Title (English): Judas Maccabaeus rededicates the temple; Festival of Dedication
Title (Tamil): கிரேக்க விக்கிரகாராதனையால் தீட்டுப்படுத்தப்பட்டபின் ஆலய மறுபிரதிஷ்டை; பிரதிஷ்டை பண்டிகை
Description (English): After a three-year struggle, Judas Maccabaeus recaptured the city and temple, built a new altar, and rededicated it on Chislev 25, exactly three years after its profanation; the eight-day Festival of Dedication commemorates it.
Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
Where sources differ: dp ch. 13 dates the rededication to 164 B.C.E.; si and Insight give Chislev 25, 165 B.C.E.

Title (English): Death of Antiochus IV
Description (English): Antiochus IV died in 163 B.C.E.; later Seleucid kings did not occupy the position of 'the king of the north.'
Main source: The Two Kings Change Identities

Title (English): Maccabean Jews appeal to Rome
Description (English): With the war against the Seleucids continuing, the Jews appealed to Rome for help, bringing Roman influence onto the Jerusalem scene.
Main source: Jerusalem
Where sources differ: dp ch. 13 says the Maccabees probably made a treaty with Rome in 161 B.C.E.

Title (English): Septuagint translation completed
Description (English): Translation of the entire Hebrew Scriptures into Greek was finally completed during the second century B.C.E., perhaps by 150 B.C.E.
Main source: Versions

Title (English): Rome destroys Corinth; Achaia and Macedonia become provinces
Description (English): After the Achaean League rebelled, Rome's armies destroyed Corinth and formed the province of Achaia; Macedonia also became a Roman province.
Description (Tamil): காலப்போக்கில் மக்கெதோனியா ரோமைச் சார்ந்திருக்கலாயிற்று, இறுதியாக பொ.ச.மு. 146-ல் ரோமோடு இணைந்துவிட்டது.
Main source: Greece, Greeks

Title (English): Simon Maccabaeus makes Jerusalem capital of a free region
Description (English): Simon Maccabaeus made Jerusalem the capital of a region ostensibly free from subservience or taxation to Gentile nations.
Main source: Jerusalem

Title (English): Dead Sea Scroll of Isaiah copied (125–100 B.C.E.)
Title (Tamil): சவக்கடல் சுருள்களில் இருக்கும் ஏசாயா புத்தகத்தின் 40-வது அதிகாரம் (கி.மு. 125-100 வரையான காலப்பகுதி)
Description (English): NWT Appendix A3 shows chapter 40 of Isaiah in the Dead Sea Scrolls, dated from 125 to 100 B.C.E. Compared with Hebrew manuscripts from about a thousand years later, it shows only minor differences, mostly in spelling. “All Scripture” Study 5 dates this Isaiah scroll (1QIsa) toward the end of the second century B.C.E.
Description (Tamil): சவக்கடல் சுருள்களில் இருக்கும் ஏசாயா புத்தகத்தின் 40-வது அதிகாரம் (கி.மு. 125-100 வரையான காலப்பகுதி). ஆயிரம் வருஷங்களுக்குப் பின்பு கண்டுபிடிக்கப்பட்ட எபிரெய கையெழுத்துப் பிரதிகளோடு ஒப்பிட்டுப் பார்க்கும்போது சின்னச் சின்ன வித்தியாசங்கள்தான் இருக்கின்றன, அதுவும் பெரும்பாலும் வார்த்தைகளிலுள்ள எழுத்துக்களில்தான்!
Main source: A3 How the Bible Came to Us
Notes: A3 prints the window 125–100 B.C.E. (one copying, so a 'between' point); si Study 5 par. 23 says 'toward the end of the second century B.C.E.' The Isaiah scroll was found in 1947 (b17-0010).

Title (English): John Hyrcanus I forces circumcision on the Idumeans
Description (English): According to Josephus, the Maccabean ruler John Hyrcanus I subjugated the Idumeans (Edomites) and forced circumcision on them; Herod's family were therefore nominally Jews.
Main source: Herod

Title (English): Aristobulus I takes the title of king
Description (English): Aristobulus I, Jerusalem's high priest and not of David's line, assumed the title of king, establishing a Maccabean kingdom.
Description (Tamil): 38 மக்கபேயர்கள் பொ.ச.மு. 161-ல் ரோமோடு சமாதான ஒப்பந்தம் செய்து, பொ.ச.மு. 104-ல் ஒரு ராஜ்யத்தை ஏற்படுத்தியிருக்க வேண்டும்.
Main source: Jerusalem

Title (English): Pompey makes Syria a Roman province
Description (English): Roman General Pompey made Syria a Roman province, ending the Seleucid dynasty.
Description (Tamil): இறுதியாக பொ.ச.மு. 64-ல் சிரியா ரோம மாகாணமானது.
Main source: Two Kings in Conflict

Title (English): Pompey takes Jerusalem; Rome rules
Title (Tamil): ரோம், ஆறாவது உலக வல்லரசு, எருசலேமை ஆளுகிறது
Description (English): Called in to settle the quarrel between Aristobulus II and Hyrcanus, Roman forces under Pompey besieged Jerusalem for three months and took it; Rome, the sixth world power, now ruled Jerusalem.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 63-ல் ரோம தளபதியான நேயஸ் பாம்பி, எருசலேமை மூன்று மாதம் முற்றுகையிட்டுக் கைப்பற்றினார்.
Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
Where sources differ: dp chs. 4, 9, 10 date Rome as world power 'from 30 B.C.E.' (fall of Ptolemaic Egypt); si says Rome rules Jerusalem from 63 B.C.E. Different reference points.

Title (English): Julius Caesar invades Britannia
Description (English): Roman General Julius Caesar invaded Britannia but failed to establish a permanent settlement.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 55-ல் ரோம தளபதி ஜூலியஸ் சீசர் பிரிட்டானியாமீது படையெடுத்தார், ஆனால் அவரால் ஒரு நிரந்தரமான குடியிருப்பை ஏற்படுத்த முடியவில்லை.
Main source: Who Will Rule the World?

Title (English): Lex Julia majestatis enacted
Description (English): The law called lex Julia majestatis made it an offense to engage in any activity against the sovereign power of Rome, a background to the charges later brought against Jesus.
Main source: Caesar

Title (English): Herod made governor of Galilee
Description (English): Antipater II appointed his son Herod governor of Galilee, where Herod distinguished himself by ridding the territory of robber bands.
Main source: Herod

Title (English): Julius Caesar appointed dictator
Description (English): Gaius Julius Caesar was appointed dictator of Rome for ten years.
Main source: Caesar

Title (English): Julius Caesar assassinated
Description (English): Julius Caesar was murdered by conspirators; his great-nephew Octavian was then only 18.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 44-ல் ஜூலியஸ் சீசர் கொலைசெய்யப்பட்ட போது, அவரது சகோதரியின் பேரனான கயஸ் ஆக்டேவியனுக்கு 18 வயதுதான்.
Main source: Caesar

Title (English): Herod appointed king of Judea by the Roman Senate
Description (English): On Mark Antony's recommendation, the Roman senate appointed the Edomite Herod king of greater Judea, though he could not establish himself in Jerusalem until about three years later.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 39-ல், ரோம பேரவை ஏதோமியரான ஏரோதை யூதேயாவின் ராஜாவாக்கியது.
Main source: Herod
Where sources differ: Insight 'Herod' notes Josephus' method would place the appointment in 40 B.C.E., while Appianos' data place it in 39 B.C.E.
Chart hint: Covered by span – hide on chart
Start/end of span: start of Reign of Herod the Great over Judea (b12-0038)

Title (English): Reign of Herod the Great over Judea
Description (English): The Roman Senate made the Edomite Herod king of Judea about 39 B.C.E.; three years later he took Jerusalem. He rebuilt the temple and ordered the killing of the boys of Bethlehem, and he likely died in 1 B.C.E.
Main source: Herod
Where sources differ: Insight “Jerusalem” says Herod “did not get control of Jerusalem until 37 or 36 B.C.E., from which date his rule effectively began.”

Title (English): Herod takes Jerusalem by storm
Title (Tamil): ஏரோது (ரோம் நியமித்த அரசன்) மூர்க்கத் தாக்குதலால் எருசலேமைக் கைப்பற்றுகிறார்
Description (English): Herod, appointed king by Rome, took Jerusalem and deposed Antigonus, ending Maccabean rule; his rule effectively began from this date.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 37-ல் எருசலேமை இவர் கைப்பற்றவே, மக்கபேயர்களின் ஆட்சி முடிவுக்கு வந்தது.
Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
Where sources differ: Insight 'Herod' notes Josephus also says it was 27 years after Pompey's capture (63), which would make it 36 B.C.E.; Insight 'Jerusalem' says '37 or 36'.

Title (English): Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra at Actium
Description (English): At the battle of Actium, Octavian defeated the combined forces of Cleopatra VII and Mark Antony and emerged as the undisputed ruler of the Roman Empire.
Description (Tamil): (தானியேல் 11:14) பொ.ச.மு. 31-ல், ஆக்டியம் யுத்தத்தின்போது, தாலமிய வம்சத்தின் கடைசி ராணியான ஏழாம் க்ளியோபாட்ரா, அவளது ரோம காதலன் மார்க் ஆன்டனி ஆகிய இருவரது ஒன்றிணைந்த படைகளையும் ரோம அரசரான ஆக்டேவியன் வீழ்த்தினார்.
Main source: Augustus
Start/end of span: start of Reign of Augustus (Octavian), Roman emperor (b12-0039)

Title (English): Reign of Augustus (Octavian), Roman emperor
Description (English): Octavian became undisputed ruler of the Roman Empire after Actium in 31 B.C.E. and received the title Augustus in 27 B.C.E.; his registration decree brought Jesus’ birth at Bethlehem. He died in 14 C.E.
Main source: Caesar
Where sources differ: Insight “Chronology” counts “Augustus’ rule ran from 27 B.C.E. to 14 C.E.” (from his title Augustus); the Insight “Caesar” table starts it in 31 B.C.E.

Title (English): Ptolemaic Egypt falls to Rome
Description (English): The Ptolemaic dynasty, last of the four Hellenistic kingdoms, fell to Rome; by 30 B.C.E. Rome had supremacy over Syria and Egypt and emerged as the world power of Bible prophecy.
Description (Tamil): தாலமியின் ராஜ வம்சம், பொ.ச.மு. 30-ல் எகிப்தை ரோம் கைப்பற்றியது வரை ஆட்சியில் இருந்தது.
Main source: Who Will Rule the World?
Start/end of span: end of Greece, fifth world power (b12-0037); start of Rome, sixth world power (b12-0040)

Title (English): Rome, sixth world power
Description (English): By 30 B.C.E. Rome had taken over all the Hellenistic kingdoms and become the sixth world power; it executed Jesus, persecuted his disciples, and destroyed Jerusalem in 70 C.E.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 30-ம் ஆண்டிற்குள், ரோம் எல்லா கிரேக்க ராஜ்யங்களையும் வென்று, பைபிள் சரித்திரத்தின் ஆறாம் உலக வல்லரசானது.
Main source: Who Can Stand Against the Prince of Princes?
Notes: jw.org gives no single end date for the Roman World Power. End sort_key 1763 is an ordering estimate only: dp chap. 10 says that by 1763 the British Empire had become the seventh world power.

Title (English): Octavian given the title Augustus
Description (English): The Roman Senate bestowed on Octavian the title 'Augustus'; he became the first emperor of Rome, known as Caesar Augustus, whose rule ran from 27 B.C.E. to 14 C.E.
Description (Tamil): மேலும், பொ.ச.மு. 27, ஜனவரி 16 அன்று, பேரவை ஆக்டேவியனுக்கு “அகஸ்டஸ்” என்ற பட்டப்பெயர் சூட்டியது.
Main source: Augustus
Where sources differ: Insight 'Rome' gives Octavian's sole rule as 31 B.C.E.-14 C.E.; Insight 'Chronology' counts Augustus' rule from 27 B.C.E.

Title (English): Province of Achaia includes all southern and central Greece
Description (English): By 27 B.C.E. the Roman province of Achaia came to include all of southern and central Greece.
Main source: Greece, Greeks

Title (English): Herod begins rebuilding the temple
Description (English): According to Josephus, Herod began rebuilding Zerubbabel's temple in the 18th year of his reign, which could mean 18/17 B.C.E. The sanctuary took 18 months and other main structures eight years, but work continued long after.
Main source: Herod
Where sources differ: Insight 'Temple' notes Josephus' Jewish War says the 15th year, while Jewish Antiquities says the 18th (the generally accepted figure).
Start/end of span: start of Herod’s rebuilding of the temple (b12-0041)

Title (English): Herod’s rebuilding of the temple
Description (English): Herod began rebuilding Zerubbabel’s temple in the 18th year of his reign; the sanctuary took 18 months, but work on the courts and buildings went on for decades and was finished only a few years before the Romans destroyed the temple.
Main source: Herod
Computed by pipeline: Insight “Temple” says the work “was not finished until about six years before the destruction of the temple in 70 C.E.”; the end is shown as c. 64 C.E. (70 − 6). No jw.org page prints 64.

Title (English): Augustus becomes Pontifex Maximus
Description (English): After the death of Lepidus, Augustus assumed the title 'Pontifex Maximus' (high priest).
Main source: Augustus

Title (English): Angel Gabriel foretells the birth of John the Baptist to Zechariah
Title (Tamil): யோவான் ஸ்நானகருடைய பிறப்பைப் பற்றி காபிரியேல் தூதர் சகரியாவிடம் முன்னறிவிக்கிறார்
Description (English): Angel Gabriel foretells the birth of John the Baptist to Zechariah. The place is given as Jerusalem, temple. NWT Study Edition Appendix A7-A (“Leading Up to Jesus’ Ministry”) dates this to 3 B.C.E..
Description (Tamil): யோவான் ஸ்நானகருடைய பிறப்பைப் பற்றி காபிரியேல் தூதர் சகரியாவிடம் முன்னறிவிக்கிறார் — எருசலேம், ஆலயம்
Main source: A7-A Main Events of Jesus’ Earthly Life—Leading Up to Jesus’ Ministry
Where sources differ: Wording in pre-2013 Insight chart (it-2 'Jesus Christ', par 124): “Birth of John the Baptizer foretold to Zechariah”.

Title (English): Augustus given the title 'Father of His Country'
Description (English): In 2 B.C.E., the year of Jesus' birth, the Roman Senate gave Augustus the title Pater Patriae.
Description (Tamil): பொ.ச.மு. 2-ல், அதாவது இயேசு பிறந்த வருடத்தில், பேரவை அவருக்கு “தன் நாட்டின் தந்தை” என அர்த்தப்படுத்தும் பாடர் பாட்ரியை என்ற பட்டம் சூட்டியது.
Main source: The Two Kings Change Identities

Description (Tamil): வரவிருந்த ஒரு கொடிய பஞ்சத்தைக் குறித்து ‘ஆவியின் மூலமாய்’ அகபு தீர்க்கதரிசனம் உரைத்தது ... ஏரோதின் மரணத்துக்குச் சற்று முன்பே நடந்தன.
Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time

Title (English): Disciples first called Christians at Antioch
Description (English): After Barnabas brought Saul from Tarsus, the two taught in Antioch for a whole year, and there the disciples were by divine providence first called Christians—possibly as early as 44 C.E.
Main source: Acts Study Notes—Chapter 11

Title (English): Apostle James (son of Zebedee) executed by Herod Agrippa I
Description (English): Herod Agrippa I had the apostle James, John’s brother, put to death with the sword; he was the first of the 12 apostles to die as a martyr.
Description (Tamil): சீஷனாகிய யாக்கோபு பட்டயத்தால் கொல்லப்பட்டது ... பொ.ச. 44-ஐ இந்த எல்லா நிகழ்ச்சிகளுக்குமுரிய காலமாக குறிக்கலாம்.

Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time

Title (English): Peter imprisoned and miraculously released by an angel
Title (Tamil): பேதுரு சிறையில் அடைக்கப்படுகிறார், அற்புதமாக விடுதலை செய்யப்படுகிறார்
Description (English): Herod Agrippa I jailed Peter at Passover time intending to execute him, but while the congregation prayed intensely, Jehovah’s angel led him out of the prison.

Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time

Title (English): Herod Agrippa I dies, struck by Jehovah’s angel
Description (English): At Caesarea, after accepting acclaim as a god, Herod Agrippa I was struck by Jehovah’s angel and died, aged 54, having reigned three years over all Judea.

Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time

Description (English): The great famine foretold by Agabus came about 46 C.E., during the reign of Claudius; Josephus also refers to it.
Description (Tamil): முன்னறிவிக்கப்பட்ட இந்தப் பஞ்சம் ஏறக்குறைய பொ.ச. 46-⁠ல் ஏற்பட்டது.
Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time

Title (English): Paul and Barnabas carry famine relief from Antioch to Jerusalem

Title (English): Paul’s first missionary journey
Description (English): Set aside by holy spirit at Syrian Antioch, Paul and Barnabas (with John Mark at first) sailed from Seleucia to Cyprus and preached in many cities of Asia Minor, probably from the spring of 47 to the autumn of 48 C.E.

Title (English): Circumcision issue raised at Antioch
Description (English): Men from Judea came to Antioch claiming that non-Jewish believers had to be circumcised to be saved; Paul and Barnabas disputed this and were sent to Jerusalem.
Description (Tamil): விருத்தசேதனம் சம்பந்தமாக அந்தியோகியாவில் பிரச்சினை.

Title (English): Governing body in Jerusalem rules against requiring circumcision of Gentile believers
Title (Tamil): புறஜாதியாரில் விசுவாசிகளானோருக்கு விருத்தசேதனம் தேவையில்லையென ஆளும் குழு தீர்மானிக்கிறது
Description (English): The apostles and older men in Jerusalem, after testimony by Peter, Barnabas, and Paul and a Scriptural conclusion offered by James, decided that circumcision was not required of believers from the nations; the decree was delivered to Antioch.
Description (Tamil): புறஜாதியாரில் விசுவாசிகளானோருக்கு விருத்தசேதனம் தேவையில்லையென ஆளும் குழு தீர்மானிக்கிறது.
People: Peter; Paul; Barnabas; James (Jesus’ brother); John
Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time

Title (English): Paul corrects Peter at Antioch
Description (English): At Syrian Antioch, Paul publicly corrected Peter for withdrawing from Gentile believers out of fear of those from Jerusalem.
Description (Tamil): பேதுருவை பவுல் கண்டிக்கிறார் (கலா. 2:11-14).
Main source: “Go . . . and Make Disciples” (box: Important Dates in the Spread of Christianity During the First Century C.E.)

Title (English): Paul’s second missionary journey
Description (English): Leaving Syrian Antioch with Silas in the summer of 49 C.E., Paul traveled through Asia Minor, crossed into Europe, founded congregations in Macedonia and Greece, stayed 18 months in Corinth, and returned to Antioch probably in the summer of 52 C.E.
Description (Tamil): பவுலின் இரண்டாவது மிஷனரி பயணம், ஏ. பொ.ச. 49-52. ... அவர் அங்கிருந்து இரண்டாவது பயணம் சென்றபோது அது பொ.ச. 49-⁠ன் கோடைகாலமாய் இருந்திருக்க வேண்டும்.
Places: Antioch (Syria); Lystra; Troas; Philippi; Thessalonica; Beroea; Athens; Corinth; Ephesus; Caesarea
Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time

Title (English): Barnabas and Mark preach in Cyprus
Description (English): After a sharp disagreement over taking Mark along, Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus while Paul chose Silas.
Description (Tamil): சீப்புருவில் பர்னபாவும் மாற்குவும் பிரசங்கிக்கிறார்கள்.
Main source: “Go . . . and Make Disciples” (box: Important Dates in the Spread of Christianity During the First Century C.E.)

Title (English): Claudius expels the Jews from Rome
Description (English): Emperor Claudius ordered all Jews to leave Rome, an edict that brought Aquila and Priscilla to Corinth shortly before Paul arrived there.

Title (English): Timothy joins Paul at Lystra
Description (English): On his second tour Paul came to Lystra, apparently Timothy’s hometown, and arranged for the well-reported young disciple Timothy to travel with him.
Main source: Acts Study Notes—Chapter 16

Title (English): Paul’s vision of the Macedonian man; Paul crosses into Europe
Description (English): At Troas Paul saw in vision a man of Macedonia pleading for help; probably in the spring of 50 C.E. he answered the call and crossed over into Europe.

Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time

Title (English): Luke joins Paul at Troas
Description (English): The physician Luke, writer of Acts, began accompanying Paul at Troas, as shown by the narrative’s change to “we,” and went with him as far as Philippi.

Main source: “Go . . . and Make Disciples” (box: Important Dates in the Spread of Christianity During the First Century C.E.)

Title (English): Paul visits Philippi
Description (English): Paul and his companions preached in Philippi, a Roman colony in Macedonia, where they were beaten and imprisoned before the jailer and his household became believers.
Description (Tamil): பிலிப்பி பட்டணத்துக்கு பவுல் போகிறார்.
Main source: “Go . . . and Make Disciples” (box: Important Dates in the Spread of Christianity During the First Century C.E.)

Title (English): Lydia and her household become Christians in Philippi
Description (English): Lydia, a seller of purple, and her household were baptized in Philippi, among the first in Europe to embrace Christianity through Paul’s preaching.
Main source: Acts Study Notes—Chapter 16

Title (English): Philippian congregation founded
Description (English): A congregation was established in Philippi, the first in Europe resulting from Paul’s work.
Description (Tamil): பிலிப்பி சபை உருவாகிறது.
Main source: “Go . . . and Make Disciples” (box: Important Dates in the Spread of Christianity During the First Century C.E.)

Title (English): Thessalonian congregation founded
Description (English): Paul reasoned from the Scriptures in the synagogue of Thessalonica for three sabbaths; some believed and a congregation was formed despite mob opposition.
Description (Tamil): தெசலோனிக்கே சபை உருவாகிறது.
Main source: “Go . . . and Make Disciples” (box: Important Dates in the Spread of Christianity During the First Century C.E.)

Title (English): Paul preaches in Athens
Description (English): After Beroea, Paul came to Athens, reasoning in the synagogue and marketplace and giving his speech at the Areopagus.
Description (Tamil): அத்தேனே பட்டணத்துக்கு பவுல் வருகிறார்.
Main source: “Go . . . and Make Disciples” (box: Important Dates in the Spread of Christianity During the First Century C.E.)

Title (English): Gallio serves as proconsul of Achaia

Title (English): Paul brought before Gallio’s judgment seat and released
Description (English): While Gallio was proconsul, the Jews of Corinth brought Paul before the judgment seat, but Gallio dismissed the case; Paul stayed “quite some days longer” and then sailed for Syria in the spring of 52.

Title (English): Felix becomes procurator of Judea
Description (English): Most scholars date the start of Antonius Felix’s sole procuratorship of Judea to 52 C.E.; Tacitus indicates he served earlier jointly with Cumanus.
Main source: Felix

Title (English): Apollos taught by Aquila and Priscilla in Ephesus
Description (English): The eloquent Alexandrian Jew Apollos, who knew only John’s baptism, was taught the way of God more accurately by Aquila and Priscilla in Ephesus and went on to help the brothers in Achaia.
Main source: Acts Study Notes—Chapter 18

Title (English): Paul returns to Syrian Antioch, ending his second journey
Description (English): After sailing from Corinth via Ephesus to Caesarea and greeting the congregation, apparently in Jerusalem, Paul arrived back at Syrian Antioch, probably in the summer of 52 C.E.

Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time

Title (English): Nero becomes Roman emperor
Description (English): After Claudius died in 54 C.E., Nero, his adopted son, took the throne at about 17; all references to Caesar in Acts chapters 25 to 28 apply to him.

Description (Tamil): பொ.ச. 64 ஜூலையில் ரோம் நகரமே தீப்பற்றி எரிந்து பெரிய நாசத்தை ஏற்படுத்தியது. அந்த நகரத்தின் 14 பிராந்தியங்களில் 10-⁠ல் மிகுதியான சேதம் ஏற்பட்டிருந்தது.
Main source: Bible Book Number 55—2 Timothy

Title (English): Nero’s persecution of Christians
Description (English): Following the fire, Nero fastened the guilt on the Christians, and a fierce persecution with cruel executions burst upon them in Rome.
Description (Tamil): ரோமில் பெருந்தீ பற்றியெரிந்த தேதி பொ.ச. 64-⁠ன் ஜூலை மாதம் என உலக சரித்திரம் குறிப்பிடுகிறது. இதைப் பின்தொடர்ந்து திடீரென கிறிஸ்தவர்களை நீரோ துன்புறுத்தத் தொடங்கினான்.
Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time

Title (English): Writing of 2 Timothy completed
Description (English): The writing of 2 Timothy was completed c. 65 C.E. Writer: Paul; place written: Rome.
Description (Tamil): 2 தீமோத்தேயு: எழுதியவர்(கள்): பவுல்; எழுதப்பட்ட இடம்: ரோம்; முடிக்கப்பட்ட வருஷம் (கி.பி.): ஏ. 65.
Main source: Table of the Books of the Bible
Notes: Writer(s): Paul. Place written: Rome. Writing completed: c. 65 C.E. Time covered: —. si par. 3: probably written about 65 C.E., immediately prior to Paul's martyrdom.

Title (English): Writing of Jude completed
Description (English): The writing of Jude was completed c. 65 C.E. Writer: Jude (Jesus’ brother); place written: Israel (?).
Description (Tamil): யூதா: எழுதியவர்(கள்): யூதா (இயேசுவின் சகோதரர்); எழுதப்பட்ட இடம்: இஸ்ரவேல் (?); முடிக்கப்பட்ட வருஷம் (கி.பி.): ஏ. 65.
Main source: Table of the Books of the Bible

Title (English): Paul’s second imprisonment in Rome
Title (Tamil): ரோமில் இரண்டாம் முறையாக பவுல் சிறையில் அடைக்கப்படுகிறார்
Description (English): Paul was again a prisoner in Rome, this time in chains and under far more severe conditions, expecting execution; few dared to visit him, though Onesiphorus and Luke did.
Description (Tamil): பவுல் மறுபடியும் ரோமில் கைதியாக இருந்தார். எனினும், இந்த இரண்டாவது சிறையிருப்பின் சூழ்நிலைமைகள் முதலில் இருந்ததைப் பார்க்கிலும் கடுமையாக இருந்தன. இது பொ.ச. 65 ஆக இருக்கலாம்.
Main source: “Go . . . and Make Disciples” (box: Important Dates in the Spread of Christianity During the First Century C.E.)

Title (English): Titus leaves for Dalmatia
Description (English): During Paul’s final imprisonment, Titus went to Dalmatia, as Paul mentions in his second letter to Timothy.
Description (Tamil): தீத்து தல்மாத்தியாவுக்குச் செல்கிறார் (2 தீ. 4:10).
Main source: “Go . . . and Make Disciples” (box: Important Dates in the Spread of Christianity During the First Century C.E.)

Title (English): Jude written
Description (English): Jude (Jesus’ brother) completed the letter Jude at Palestine (?), about 65 C.E.
Description (Tamil): எழுத்தாளர்: யூதா; எழுதப்பட்ட இடம்: பலஸ்தீனா (?); எழுதி முடிக்கப்பட்டது: ஏ. பொ.ச. 65.
Main source: Table of the Books of the Bible

Title (English): Paul executed in Rome
Description (English): Paul likely suffered martyrdom at the hands of Nero shortly after his final imprisonment in Rome, about 65 C.E., having finished the race faithfully.
Description (Tamil): ஏறக்குறைய பொ.ச. 65-⁠ல் ரோமில் கடைசியாக சிறையிருந்தபோது, சீக்கிரத்திலேயே நீரோவின் கைகளில் பவுல் இரத்தசாட்சியாக மரித்திருக்கலாம்.
Main source: “Go . . . and Make Disciples” (box: Important Dates in the Spread of Christianity During the First Century C.E.)

Title (English): Jewish revolt against Rome begins
Description (English): In 66 C.E. the Jews rose in revolt against Roman rule; revolutionaries massacred the Roman garrisons at Masada and Jerusalem, bringing the wrath of Rome on the nation.
Main source: Jerusalem
Start/end of span: start of Jewish revolt against Rome (b12-0050)

Title (English): Jewish revolt against Rome
Description (English): The Jewish revolt broke out in 66 C.E., two years before Nero’s death, and was suppressed when Roman armies destroyed Jerusalem in 70 C.E., in the reign of Vespasian.
Main source: Caesar
Notes: The last stronghold, Masada, fell in 73 C.E. (b6-0097).

Title (English): Sicarii (“dagger men”) seize Masada and massacre the Roman garrison
Description (English): A band of Sicarii under Eleazar, son of Jairus, seized the fortress of Masada and massacred its Roman garrison—what Josephus called the true beginning of the war with Rome.
Main source: Dagger Men

Title (English): Cestius Gallus surrounds Jerusalem, then suddenly withdraws
Description (English): Before 66 C.E. ended, Roman forces under Cestius Gallus surrounded Jerusalem and pushed up to the temple walls—the “disgusting thing” standing in a holy place—then withdrew for no apparent reason, giving Christians the signal to flee.
Main source: Jerusalem

Title (English): Christians flee from Jerusalem and Judea to Pella
Description (English): Heeding Jesus’ warning, Christians used the Roman withdrawal to flee; according to Eusebius they went from Jerusalem and Judea across the Jordan to Pella, a city in the mountainous Decapolis/Perea region.
Description (Tamil): யூசிபியஸ் சொல்கிறபடி, யூதேயாவிலும் எருசலேமிலும் இருந்த கிறிஸ்தவர்கள் யோர்தான் ஆற்றைக் கடந்து பெல்லா நகரத்துக்குத் தப்பியோடினார்கள்; அந்த நகரம் தெக்கப்போலியில் இருந்த ஒரு மலைப்பிரதேசத்தில் அமைந்திருந்தது.
Main source: Jerusalem
Notes: Tamil description is the Tamil Study Edition note on Matt. 24:16 (no year stated in that note); title_ta left null because no Tamil heading exists for this event.

Title (English): Reign of Galba, Roman emperor
Description (English): Galba briefly ruled after Nero’s death.
Main source: Caesar

Title (English): Nero commits suicide
Description (English): Condemned by the Senate during a revolt, Emperor Nero, who had ruled from 54 C.E., committed suicide in 68 C.E. at about the age of 31.
Main source: Caesar
Chart hint: Covered by span – hide on chart
Start/end of span: end of Reign of Nero, Roman emperor (b12-0049)

Title (English): Reign of Vespasian, Roman emperor
Description (English): During Vespasian’s reign the Jewish revolt was crushed and Jerusalem was destroyed in 70 C.E.
Main source: Caesar

Title (English): Roman armies under Titus lay siege to Jerusalem
Description (English): Roman forces under General Titus returned in greater numbers and besieged Jerusalem, then crowded with Passover celebrants, throwing up siege banks and a wall around the city.
Main source: Jerusalem
Start/end of span: start of Roman siege and conquest of Jerusalem (b12-0053)

Title (English): Roman siege and conquest of Jerusalem
Description (English): Roman forces under General Titus besieged Jerusalem, crowded with Passover celebrants, and conquered it in 4 months and 25 days, destroying the city and its temple.
Main source: Jerusalem

Title (English): Jerusalem and its temple destroyed by the Romans
Description (English): In just 4 months and 25 days, from April 3 to August 30, 70 C.E., the Romans conquered Jerusalem, destroying the city and its temple as Jesus had foretold; genealogical records were lost.
Description (Tamil): எருசலேமும் அதன் ஆலயமும் ரோமரால் அழிக்கப்பட்டன. இயேசுவின் தீர்க்கதரிசனம் கி.பி. 70-ல் குறிப்பிடத்தக்க விதத்தில் நிறைவேறியது. அப்போது ரோமர்கள் எருசலேமை அழித்தார்கள்.
Main source: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
Start/end of span: end of Jewish revolt against Rome (b12-0050); end of Roman siege and conquest of Jerusalem (b12-0053)

Title (English): Masada, the last Jewish stronghold, falls to the Romans
Description (English): The Sicarii at Masada defied Rome until 73 C.E., when its defenses were breached; to avoid capture the defenders carried out a mass suicide, ending the Jewish war.
Main source: Matthew Study Notes—Chapter 24

Title (English): Reign of Titus, Roman emperor
Description (English): Titus, who as general had besieged and destroyed Jerusalem in 70 C.E., ruled as emperor for two years.
Main source: Caesar

Title (English): Reign of Domitian, Roman emperor
Description (English): Domitian was a harsh opponent of Christianity; during his rule the apostle John was exiled to Patmos.
Main source: Caesar

Title (English): Persecution under Emperor Domitian peaks
Description (English): Persecution of Christians reached a peak during Domitian’s rule (81-96 C.E.), particularly in its last three years; John’s exile to Patmos is generally placed in this reign.
Description (Tamil): அப்போஸ்தலன் யோவான் எழுதின ஐந்து புத்தகங்கள், பேரரசன் டொமீஷியன் கொண்டுவந்த துன்புறுத்தல் காலத்தின் முடிவில் எழுதப்பட்டன. இந்த அரசனுடைய ஆட்சிக்காலம் பொ.ச. 81-96 வரையாகும்.
Main source: Chronology

Title (English): Reign of Nerva, Roman emperor
Description (English): Nerva ruled briefly after Domitian.
Main source: Caesar

Title (English): Writing of Revelation completed
Description (English): The writing of Revelation was completed c. 96 C.E. Writer: the apostle John; place written: Patmos.

Title (English): Apostle John exiled on Patmos receives the Revelation
Description (English): In very old age John was exiled to the island of Patmos “for speaking about God and bearing witness to Jesus,” and there he received and wrote down the Revelation, about 96 C.E.
Description (Tamil): பத்மு தீவுக்கு நாடுகடத்தப்பட்டபோது யோவான், ஏறக்குறைய பொ.ச. 96-ல் வெளிப்படுத்துதலை எழுதினார்.

Description (English): According to ancient tradition, John was released after Domitian died in 96 C.E., evidently by his successor Nerva (96-98 C.E.), and went to Ephesus.
