Title (English): Life of João Ferreira de Almeida
Description (English): João Ferreira de Almeida: from João Ferreira de Almeida, Portuguese Bible translator, born (1628) to Almeida dies while translating Ezekiel (1691). Dates as given in the cited jw.org publications.
Main source: The First Bible in Portuguese—A Story of Perseverance
Computed by pipeline: Built from b7-0165 (start) and b7-0172 (end).

Title (English): Dutch Statenvertaling published
Description (English): The Dutch Statenvertaling of 1637, based on the Received Text, appears in the si chart of leading translations.
Description (Tamil): ஸ்டேட்டென்வெர்ட்டலிங் 1637 M ஹீரே ரிசீவ்ட் டெக்ஸ்ட்
Main source: Study Number 7—The Bible in Modern Times

Title (English): Bay Psalm Book uses "Iehovah"
Description (English): The Bay Psalm Book, the first literature published in England's American colonies (printed 1640), translated the Psalms from Hebrew and used the divine name, as at Psalm 1:2 and 83:18.
Description (Tamil): 1640-ல் அச்சிடப்பட்ட அதன் மூலப் பிரதியில், சங்கீத புத்தகம் உள்ளது; அது எபிரெயுவிலிருந்து அன்றைய ஆங்கிலத்தில் மொழிபெயர்க்கப்பட்டிருந்தது.
Main source: This Is Our Spiritual Heritage

Title (English): Peace of Westphalia ends the Thirty Years' War
Description (English): The Treaty of Westphalia in 1648 ended the Thirty Years' War and granted equal recognition to Catholic, Lutheran, and Calvinist religions; Pope Innocent X declared it null and void.
Description (Tamil): 1648-⁠ல் இந்த ஒப்பந்தம் கையெழுத்தானபோது அது முப்பதாண்டு கால போருக்கு முற்றுப்புள்ளி வைத்தது; தனி நாடுகள் அடங்கிய கண்டமாக நவீன ஐரோப்பா பிறப்பதற்கும் வழிவகுத்தது.
Main source: The Peace of Westphalia—A Turning Point in Europe

Title (English): Inquisition at Goa sentences Almeida to death in absentia
Description (English): Almeida's exposure of church doctrine led to clashes with Catholic missionaries; in 1661 an Inquisitional court at Goa, India, sentenced him to death for heresy and burned him in effigy.
Description (Tamil): 1661-⁠ல், இந்தியாவிலுள்ள கோவாவில் இருந்த ஒடுக்குமுறை நீதிமன்றம் அவருடைய மாறுபட்ட கொள்கையின் நிமித்தம் அவருக்கு மரண தண்டனை விதித்தபோது இந்த மோதல்கள் உச்சத்தை எட்டின.
Main source: The First Bible in Portuguese—A Story of Perseverance

Title (English): Matthew's Gospel rendered into Tamil on palm leaves
Description (English): In 1665 Matthew's Gospel was rendered into Tamil by a Dutch missionary in Ceylon (Sri Lanka); it circulated handwritten on palmyra-palm leaves rather than printed.
Main source: Translating the Bible in India

Title (English): Almeida's Portuguese "New Testament" printed
Description (English): Despite opposition from the Batavia consistory, Almeida's Portuguese New Testament went to press in Amsterdam in 1681, though revisers had altered it.
Description (Tamil): அவருடைய பைபிள் பிரசுரிக்கப்படுவதைத் தடுக்க சர்ச் ஆலோசனைக் குழு பல முயற்சிகள் எடுத்தபோதிலும், 1681-⁠ல் அவருடைய புதிய ஏற்பாடு ஆம்ஸ்டர்டாமிலுள்ள அச்சகத்தில் பிரசுரிக்கப்பட்டது.
Main source: The First Bible in Portuguese—A Story of Perseverance

Title (English): Almeida dies while translating Ezekiel
Title (Tamil): வருத்தகரமாக, 1691-⁠ல் எசேக்கியேல் புத்தகத்தின் கடைசி அதிகாரத்தை மொழிபெயர்க்கையில் அவர் இறந்துபோனார்
Description (English): Almeida died in 1691 while working on the final chapter of Ezekiel in his translation of the Hebrew Scriptures.
Description (Tamil): வருத்தகரமாக, 1691-⁠ல் எசேக்கியேல் புத்தகத்தின் கடைசி அதிகாரத்தை மொழிபெயர்க்கையில் அவர் இறந்துபோனார்.
Main source: The First Bible in Portuguese—A Story of Perseverance
Chart hint: Covered by span – hide on chart
Start/end of span: end of Life of João Ferreira de Almeida (d1-0027)

Title (English): Ziegenbalg and a fellow German land at Tranquebar to translate the Bible into Tamil
Description (English): In 1706 two Germans eager to translate the Bible into Tamil landed at the Danish trading station of Tranquebar (Tamil Nadu). One of them, Ziegenbalg, learned Tamil by tracing letters in the dust with children.
Main source: Translating the Bible in India

Title (English): Third edition of Almeida's New Testament financed for Tranquebar missionaries
Description (English): In 1711 the Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge financed a third edition of Almeida's New Testament at the request of Danish missionaries working in Tranquebar, southern India.
Description (Tamil): ஆனால் கிறிஸ்தவ அறிவைப் பரப்புவதற்கான லண்டன் சங்கமே 1711-⁠ல் ஆல்மேடாவுடைய புதிய ஏற்பாட்டின் மூன்றாம் பதிப்பை வெளியிடுவதற்கு நிதியுதவி அளித்தது; தென்னிந்தியாவைச் சேர்ந்த ட்ரான்கூபாரில் இருந்த டேனிஷ் மிஷனரிகளின் கோரிக்கைக்கு இணங்கியே அவ்வாறு செய்தது.
Main source: The First Bible in Portuguese—A Story of Perseverance

Title (English): Ziegenbalg produces the Christian Greek Scriptures in Tamil
Description (English): By the year 1714, Ziegenbalg had produced the Christian Greek Scriptures ("New Testament") in Tamil.
Main source: Translating the Bible in India
Notes: The orchestrator brief mentioned NT 1715; the only jw.org source found (Awake! 1979 6/8) says "by the year 1714". No jw.org source giving 1715 was found.

Title (English): Ziegenbalg dies, having translated the Hebrew Scriptures up to Ruth
Description (English): At his death in 1719, Ziegenbalg had completed the Tamil Hebrew Scriptures up to the book of Ruth.
Main source: Translating the Bible in India

Title (English): Complete Bible in Tamil appears
Description (English): The complete Bible in Tamil appeared in 1728. It was later revised by Philip Fabricius, whose version, known as the "Golden Version," became the basis of later Tamil revisions.
Main source: Translating the Bible in India

Title (English): Benjamin Schultze finishes a Telugu rendering (never printed)
Description (English): German scholar Benjamin Schultze evidently finished a Telugu rendering by 1732, but it was never printed; the manuscript was apparently mislaid in Halle, Germany.
Main source: Translating the Bible in India

Title (English): Alexander Cruden's Bible concordance
Title (Tamil): உதாரணமாக, 1737-⁠ல் அலெக்ஸாந்தர் க்ரூடன் இப்படிப்பட்ட நூலை உண்டாக்கினார்
Description (English): The chapter-and-verse system made possible Bible concordances such as Alexander Cruden's in 1737.
Description (Tamil): உதாரணமாக, 1737-⁠ல் அலெக்ஸாந்தர் க்ரூடன் இப்படிப்பட்ட நூலை உண்டாக்கினார்.
Main source: Study Number 6—The Christian Greek Text of the Holy Scriptures

Title (English): Kennicott publishes readings of over 600 Hebrew manuscripts
Description (English): Critical study of the Hebrew text began in the 18th century; at Oxford in 1776-1780 Benjamin Kennicott published variant readings from over 600 Masoretic Hebrew manuscripts.
Description (Tamil): 1776-80-⁠ல், ஆக்ஸ்ஃபர்ட்டில், பென்ஜமின் கென்னிக்காட் 600-⁠க்கும் மேற்பட்ட எபிரெய கையெழுத்துப் பிரதிகளின் பல்வேறு வாசகங்களைப் பிரசுரித்தார்.
Main source: Manuscripts of the Bible

Title (English): Spanish Inquisition permits Bibles with annotations
Description (English): In 1782 the Inquisition tribunal decreed that the Bible could be published in Spain provided it included annotations on history and dogma.
Description (Tamil): கடைசியாக, 1782-ல் கத்தோலிக்க சமய தீர்ப்பு மன்றத்தின் தீர்ப்பாயம் பைபிளானது சரித்திரம் மற்றும் சமயக் கொள்கை ஆகியவற்றின் பேரில் குறிப்புரைகளைக் கொண்டிருக்கும் வரையில் அது பிரசுரிக்கப்படலாம் என்று ஆணை பிறப்பித்தது.
Main source: The Spanish Bible’s Battle for Survival

Title (English): De Rossi publishes comparisons of Hebrew manuscripts at Parma
Description (English): From 1784 to 1798, Italian scholar Giambernardo de Rossi published at Parma comparisons of hundreds of Hebrew manuscripts.
Description (Tamil): பின்பு, 1784-98-⁠ல், பர்மாவில், இத்தாலிய அறிஞர் ஜே. பி. டீ ரோஸை, இன்னும் 800-⁠க்கும் மேற்பட்ட கையெழுத்துப் பிரதிகளின் பல்வேறு வாசகங்களைப் பிரசுரித்தார்.
Main source: Manuscripts of the Bible
Where sources differ: Insight says de Rossi compared 731 manuscripts; "All Scripture" Study 5 says variant readings of over 800 more manuscripts.

Title (English): Bishop Scio's Spanish Bible from the Vulgate
Description (English): In 1790 the Catholic bishop of Segovia, Felipe Scio de San Miguel, translated a Spanish Bible from the Latin Vulgate; it was expensive and obscure.
Description (Tamil): 1790-ல் செகோவியாவின் கத்தோலிக்க ஆயர் ஃபெலிப் சியோ டி சான் மைக்குவல், லத்தீன் வல்கேட்-ஐ பயன்படுத்தி பைபிளை ஸ்பானிய மொழியில் மொழிபெயர்த்தார்.
Main source: The Spanish Bible’s Battle for Survival

Title (English): William Carey sails for India
Description (English): Despite rebukes from predestinarian churchmen, William Carey sailed for India in 1793. With associates he eventually translated all or part of the Bible into dozens of Indian languages.
Description (Tamil): இருப்பினும் கேரி 1793-ல் இந்தியாவுக்கு கப்பலில் வந்துசேர்ந்தார்.
Main source: Part Three—How the Bible Came to Us
Where sources differ: Number of Indian languages credited to Carey varies: Watchtower 1997 10/15 says 35; Awake! 1979 6/8 says 36 (within 21 years); A Book for All People says nearly 40 (with Marshman and Ward).

Title (English): Griesbach's principal Greek master text published
Title (Tamil): கிரீஸ்பாச்சின் முழுமையான கிரேக்க வாக்கியத்தின் சிறந்த பதிப்பு 1796-1806-⁠ல் பிரசுரிக்கப்பட்டது
Description (English): J. J. Griesbach, who classified manuscripts into families, published his principal edition of the entire Greek text in 1796-1806; it later underlay Sharpe's translation and The Emphatic Diaglott.
Description (Tamil): கிரீஸ்பாச்சின் முழுமையான கிரேக்க வாக்கியத்தின் சிறந்த பதிப்பு 1796-1806-⁠ல் பிரசுரிக்கப்பட்டது.
Main source: Manuscripts of the Bible

Title (English): George Storrs born
Description (English): George Storrs, later publisher of the Bible Examiner and an advocate of conditional immortality who influenced C. T. Russell, was born on December 13, 1796.
Main source: Proclaiming the Lord’s Return (1870-1914)

Title (English): Life of George Storrs
Description (English): George Storrs: from George Storrs born (1796, December 13) to George Storrs dies (December 28, 1879). Dates as given in the cited jw.org publications.
Main source: Proclaiming the Lord’s Return (1870-1914)

Title (English): Carey sets up a printing press at Calcutta
Description (English): To publish his translations, Carey set up a primitive wooden printing press at Calcutta in 1798.
Main source: Translating the Bible in India

Title (English): Carey moves his press to Serampore
Description (English): During 1800 Carey transferred his printing establishment to the Danish settlement at Serampore, where many Bible translations were printed (over 212,000 volumes between 1801 and 1832).
Main source: Translating the Bible in India

Title (English): Mary Jones walks 25 miles for a Welsh Bible
Title (Tamil): 1800-ல், மேரி ஒரு பாதிரியாரிடமிருந்து வேல்ஸ் மொழியில் பைபிளை வாங்குவதற்காக வெறுங்காலோடு 40 கிலோமீட்டர் நடந்து சென்றாள்
Description (English): In 1800, 16-year-old Mary Jones walked barefoot 25 miles to buy a Welsh Bible. The clergyman who helped her later discussed the need for Bibles with friends in London, leading to the British and Foreign Bible Society.
Description (Tamil): 1800-ல், மேரி ஒரு பாதிரியாரிடமிருந்து வேல்ஸ் மொழியில் பைபிளை வாங்குவதற்காக வெறுங்காலோடு 40 கிலோமீட்டர் நடந்து சென்றாள்.
Main source: Part Three—How the Bible Came to Us

Title (English): Bible available in about 70 languages
Description (English): By 1800 at least portions of the Bible had appeared in 68 languages (A Book for All People) or 71 languages ("All Scripture").
Description (Tamil): 1800-க்குள், பைபிளின் பகுதிகளாவது வெளிவந்த வண்ணம் இருந்தன.
Main source: A Book That “Speaks” Living Languages
Where sources differ: "All Scripture" Study 7 gives 71 languages by 1800; A Book for All People gives 68.

Title (English): British and Foreign Bible Society founded
Title (Tamil): 81 பிரிட்டிஷ் அண்ட் ஃபாரின் பைபிள் சொஸைட்டி 1804-ல் நிறுவப்பட்டது
Description (English): The British and Foreign Bible Society was formed in London in 1804 to provide affordable Bibles in people's own languages "without note or comment." It triggered the founding of many other Bible societies.
Description (Tamil): இதன் விளைவாக 1804-ல் பிரிட்டிஷ் அண்ட் ஃபாரின் பைபிள் சொஸைட்டி தோன்றியது.
Main source: Part Three—How the Bible Came to Us

Title (English): Christian Greek Scriptures in Chinese printed at Serampore
Description (English): The Christian Greek Scriptures in Chinese came off Carey's Serampore press in 1805.
Main source: Translating the Bible in India

Title (English): Robert Morrison arrives in China to translate the Bible
Description (English): In 1807, 25-year-old Robert Morrison sailed to China, where teaching the language to foreigners was a capital offense, and secretly worked on a Chinese Bible.
Description (Tamil): 1807-ல், ராபர்ட் மாரிசன்னுக்கு 25 வயதிருக்கையில் சீனாவுக்கு வந்துசேர்ந்தார்.
Main source: They Loved the Word of God

Title (English): Entire Bible in Bengali issued
Description (English): Four years after the Chinese New Testament (1805), an entire Bible in Bengali was issued from Serampore.
Main source: Translating the Bible in India

Title (English): Adoniram and Ann Judson embark; settle in Burma (1813)
Description (English): Two weeks after their marriage in February 1812, Adoniram and Ann Judson set out, settling in Burma in 1813 to learn Burmese.
Main source: They Loved the Word of God

Title (English): Fire at Serampore destroys unpublished translations
Description (English): In 1812 a fire at the Serampore press destroyed several unpublished Bible translations, including a Telugu one; Carey quickly reorganized printing.
Main source: Translating the Bible in India

Title (English): Associate Bible societies formed in Germany, Netherlands, Denmark, and Russia
Description (English): By 1813 associate societies had been formed in Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, and Russia. Lacking translators of Hebrew and Greek, many translations sponsored by the British and Foreign Bible Society were based on the King James Version.
Description (Tamil): ஆரம்பகால உற்சாகம் வேகமாக பரவ, 1813-க்குள் துணை சங்கங்கள் ஜெர்மனியிலும் நெதர்லாந்திலும் டென்மார்க்கிலும் ரஷ்யாவிலும் தோன்றியிருந்தன.
Main source: Part Three—How the Bible Came to Us

Title (English): Morrison has the Christian Greek Scriptures in Chinese ready for printing
Description (English): In 1814, seven years after arriving in China, Morrison had the Christian Greek Scriptures ready for printing.
Description (Tamil): அவர் சீனாவுக்கு வந்துசேர்ந்து ஏழு வருடங்களுக்குப்பின், 1814-ல், கிறிஸ்தவ கிரேக்க வேதாகமத்தை அச்சிட தயாராக்கிவிட்டார்.9 இதையடுத்து, ஐந்து வருடங்களுக்குப்பின், வில்லியம் மில்லன் என்பவரின் உதவியால் அவர் எபிரெய வேதாகமத்தையும் முடித்தார்.
Main source: A Book That “Speaks” Living Languages

Title (English): Scriptures in Oriya published
Description (English): After the Serampore fire, the Scriptures in the Oriya language appeared in 1815.
Main source: Translating the Bible in India

Title (English): American Bible Society formed
Description (English): Among Bible societies formed after 1804 was the American Bible Society (1816), formed from existing local societies; by 1820 societies existed in many European lands.
Description (Tamil): a 1804 முதற்கொண்டு அமைக்கப்பட்ட பைபிள் சங்கங்களில் சில பின்வருமாறு: அமெரிக்கன் பைபிள் சொஸைட்டி (1816), இது ஏற்கெனவே அந்த வட்டாரத்தில் இருந்துவந்த சங்கங்களால் அமைக்கப்பட்டது.

Description (English): From 1871 until 1945 Germany filled the role of the king of the north: the German Empire, whose army was “swept away” in World War I (Dan. 11:25-30a), and then Nazi Germany, which attacked God’s people in the 1930’s and during World War II (Dan. 11:30b, 31a).
Description (Tamil): 1871-ல் ஜெர்மனி வடதிசை ராஜாவாக உருவெடுத்தது. ஜெர்மனி 1945 வரை வடதிசை ராஜாவாக இருந்தது.
Main source: “The King of the North” in the Time of the End
Notes: Pay Attention to Daniel’s Prophecy! (1999) ch. 15-16 listed “German Empire” (Dan. 11:27-30a) and “Hitler’s Third Reich” (Dan. 11:30b, 31) as successive kings of the north; The Watchtower, May 2020, applies Dan. 11:25-31 to Germany from 1871 to 1945.

Title (English): Bible Students Edition of the King James Version published
Description (English): The Bible Students Edition of the King James Version, with revised and enlarged Berean study helps, is published.
Main source: Printing and Distributing God’s Own Sacred Word

Title (English): Watch Tower publishes the “vow” on moral conduct
Description (English): The June 15, 1908, Watch Tower publishes a vow including the commitment to conduct oneself toward the opposite sex in private exactly as in public.
Description (Tamil): சாத்தானின் கண்ணியில் சிக்காமல் இருப்பதற்கு, ஜூன் 15, 1908, காவற்கோபுரத்தில் ஒரு உறுதிமொழி பிரசுரிக்கப்பட்டிருந்தது.
Main source: Moral Refinements—Reflecting God’s Holiness

Title (English): Magazine renamed The Watch Tower and Herald of Christ’s Presence
Description (English): The name Zion’s Watch Tower and Herald of Christ’s Presence is changed to The Watch Tower and Herald of Christ’s Presence.
Main source: Meetings for Worship, Instruction, and Encouragement

Title (English): Headquarters moved to Brooklyn, New York
Title (Tamil): உவாட்ச் டவர் சொஸைட்டியின் தலைமை அலுவலகம் நியு யார்க்கிலுள்ள புருக்லினுக்கு மாற்றப்படுகிறது
Description (English): The Society’s headquarters moves from Allegheny to Brooklyn, New York; the new home, called “Bethel,” is dedicated on January 31, 1909, with 350 present, and the move is completed in April.
Description (Tamil): உவாட்ச் டவர் சொஸைட்டியின் தலைமை அலுவலகம் நியு யார்க்கிலுள்ள புருக்லினுக்கு மாற்றப்படுகிறது
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): World headquarters in Brooklyn, New York
Description (English): The Society’s headquarters moved to Brooklyn in 1909 and remained there for over a century, apart from 1918-1919, until the Bethel family moved to the new world headquarters at Warwick, New York.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses
Where sources differ: jv says the move to Brooklyn was in April 1909; the Index 1986-2026 lists January 31, 1909.
Notes: No jw.org page found giving an exact date for leaving Brooklyn; the end is the 2016–2017 move described in the 2017 Yearbook. Operations were transferred to Pittsburgh from August 1918 to October 1919.

Title (English): Peoples Pulpit Association incorporated in New York
Description (English): Peoples Pulpit Association, later renamed Watchtower Bible and Tract Society of New York, Inc., is incorporated in connection with the move to Brooklyn.
Main source: Historic Milestones in the United States

Title (English): J. F. Rutherford admitted to the bar of the U.S. Supreme Court
Description (English): J. F. Rutherford is admitted to the bar of the United States Supreme Court, remaining a member until his death in 1942.
Main source: “Objects of Hatred by All the Nations”

Title (English): Bible Students begin to use the name International Bible Students Association
Title (Tamil): சர்வதேச பைபிள் மாணாக்கர்களின் சங்கம் என்ற பெயரை பைபிள் மாணாக்கர்கள் பயன்படுத்த ஆரம்பிக்கிறார்கள்
Description (English): The Bible Students begin using the name International Bible Students Association with reference to their meetings.
Description (Tamil): சர்வதேச பைபிள் மாணாக்கர்களின் சங்கம் என்ற பெயரை பைபிள் மாணாக்கர்கள் பயன்படுத்த ஆரம்பிக்கிறார்கள்
Main source: The Kingdom Is Born in Heaven

Title (English): Society literature reproduced in Braille
Description (English): A Bible Student in Boston and one in Canada cooperate to reproduce the Society’s literature in Braille.
Main source: Producing Bible Literature for Use in the Ministry

Title (English): Congregations send speakers to give public lecture series
Description (English): Classes (congregations) with capable speakers are encouraged to send them to surrounding towns to give a series of six public lectures.
Description (Tamil): ‘நியாயத்தீர்ப்பு,’ ‘மீட்புவிலை’ போன்ற தலைப்புகளில் ஆறு பேச்சுகளைக் கொடுப்பதற்காகச் சுற்றுவட்டாரத்தில் இருந்த பல இடங்களுக்குத் தகுதியுள்ள பேச்சாளர்களை அனுப்பும்படி ஒவ்வொரு சபைக்கும் சொல்லப்பட்டது.
Main source: Meeting Together for Worship

Title (English): Russell and six companions make round-the-world tour
Description (English): C. T. Russell and six companions travel some 35,000 miles (56,000 km) around the world to investigate the “status and prospects of Christianity” in lands including China, India, Japan, and the Philippines.

Main source: The Kingdom Is Born in Heaven

Title (English): Work begins on the “Photo-Drama of Creation”
Description (English): Russell and his associates begin work on the “Photo-Drama of Creation,” combining slides and motion pictures with sound, an educational venture far ahead of its time.
Description (Tamil): 1912-ல், “சிருஷ்டிப்பின் நிழற்பட நாடகம்”
Main source: Proclaiming the Lord’s Return (1870-1914)

Title (English): Russell’s sermons reach millions through newspapers
Description (English): By 1913 Russell’s sermons are estimated to reach 15,000,000 readers through some 2,000 newspapers in four languages.
Description (Tamil): பிரசங்கங்கள் செய்தித்தாள்களில் பிரசுரிக்கப்பட்டன, 1913-க்குள் இவை ஐக்கிய மாகாணங்கள், கனடா, மற்றும் ஐரோப்பாவில் ஆயிரக்கணக்கான செய்தித்தாள்களில் நான்கு மொழிகளில் பிரசுரமாயின.
Main source: Proclaiming the Lord’s Return (1870-1914)

Title (English): Local groups adopt the name Associated Bible Students
Description (English): To avoid confusion with the newly formed International Bible Students Association corporation, local groups adopt the name Associated Bible Students.
Main source: How We Came to Be Known as Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): 1914 report: 5,155 preaching in 43 lands
Description (English): Bible Students are active in 43 lands; 5,155 share in witnessing, and Memorial attendance is 18,243.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): First showing of the “Photo-Drama of Creation” in New York
Description (English): The “Photo-Drama of Creation” is first shown in New York on January 11 to an audience of 5,000, then in five other cities within a month; by year’s end close to (or over) 9,000,000 have seen it in North America, Europe, Australia, and New Zealand.
Description (Tamil): ஜனவரி 11-ல், “ஃபோட்டோ டிராமா ஆஃப் கிரியேஷன்” முதன்முதலில் நியு யார்க்கில் காட்டப்படுகிறது. அடுத்த மாதத்துக்குள் இன்னும் ஐந்து நகரங்களில் காட்டப்படுகிறது. அந்த வருஷத்தின் முடிவுக்குள் வட அமெரிக்கா, ஐரோப்பா, ஆஸ்திரேலியா, நியுசிலாந்து ஆகிய இடங்களில் சுமார் 90 லட்சம் பேர் அதைப் பார்க்கிறார்கள்
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses
Where sources differ: kr timeline box says “close to 9,000,000” viewers in 1914; jv events table says “over 9,000,000”.

Title (English): International Bible Students Association incorporated in London
Description (English): The International Bible Students Association, a British corporation, is incorporated in London, England.
Main source: Development of the Organization Structure

Title (English): Anglo-American dual world power, seventh world power
Description (English): During World War I the Anglo-American World Power came into being; it is the seventh world power of Bible prophecy and is still in existence.

Title (English): Convention at Saratoga Springs, New York
Description (English): A Bible Students convention is held at Saratoga Springs, New York, as some expect to receive their heavenly reward at the end of the Gentile Times.
Main source: A Time of Testing (1914-1918)

Title (English): Appointed times of the nations (Gentile Times) end
Description (English): The 'seven times' of Daniel 4, understood as 2,520 years counted from Jerusalem's overthrow in 607 B.C.E., ended in 1914, closing the 'appointed times of the nations' during which Gentile powers trampled God's Kingdom. The Watch Tower had pointed to 1914 as early as the 1870's (Insight cites the March 1880 issue).

Notes: sort_key fraction reflects kr chap. 2 timeline: in October 1914 C. T. Russell announced to the Bethel family that the Gentile times had ended. Insight Tamil mirror not available.

Title (English): Russell announces: “The Gentile times have ended”
Description (English): On Friday morning, October 2, 1914, in the Bethel dining room at Brooklyn, C. T. Russell announces: “The Gentile times have ended; their kings have had their day.”

Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): God's Kingdom born in heaven; Christ begins ruling as King
Description (English): In 1914 God's Messianic Kingdom was established in heaven, pictured in John's vision by a woman giving birth to a male child who is caught up to God's throne. No human witnessed it, but a voice in heaven announced that the Kingdom of God and the authority of his Christ had come.

Main source: What Is the Sign of “the Last Days,” or “End Times”?

Title (English): Satan hurled out of heaven down to the earth
Description (English): Shortly after Jesus was installed as Messianic King in 1914, he and his angels warred against Satan and the demons and hurled them out of heaven down to the earth. Satan is now confined to the vicinity of the earth for a short time, venting his anger on God's people.
Description (Tamil): பாம்பை, அதாவது சாத்தானை, இயேசு பூமிக்குத் தள்ளி, கொஞ்சக் காலம் அங்கே விட்டுவைத்திருக்கிறார்.—வெளிப்படுத்துதல் 12:7-9, 12.

Title (English): Last days begin; World War I breaks out and Satan's 'woe' comes upon the earth
Description (English): With Satan's greater influence on human society from 1914 (Rev. 12:12), the first world war broke out that year and the sign of Christ's presence in kingly power began to be fulfilled worldwide, marking the start of the last days of this system of things.

Title (English): World War I
Description (English): The Great War, the first world war, broke out in 1914, the year the last days began, and ended on November 11, 1918.
Main source: What Binding Satan the Devil Will Mean for Mankind

Title (English): The last days (time of the end)
Description (English): World conditions and Bible chronology show that the last days of this system began in 1914, the year World War I began; they continue until God’s Kingdom ends the present system.
Description (Tamil): 1914-ல் முதல் உலக போர் வெடித்த சமயத்தில்தான் கடைசி நாட்கள் ஆரம்பித்தது என்பதை இந்த உலக நிலைமைகளும் பைபிள் காலக்கணக்கும் தெளிவாக காட்டுகிறது.
Main source: What Is the Sign of “the Last Days,” or “End Times”?

Title (English): Harvest season begins: separating of 'wheat' from 'weeds'
Description (English): The harvest season foretold in Jesus' illustration of the wheat and the weeds began in 1914, when the time came to separate anointed Christians from imitation Christians.
Description (Tamil): 1914-ல் அறுவடைக் காலம் ஆரம்பித்தது

Start/end of span: end of Wheat and weeds grow together until the harvest (b17-0002); start of The harvest season: separating wheat from weeds (b12-0070)

Title (English): The harvest season: separating wheat from weeds
Description (English): The harvest season of Jesus’ illustration of the wheat and the weeds began in 1914, when the time came to separate faithful anointed Christians from imitation Christians and to gather the remaining anointed.
Description (Tamil): களைகளான போலிக் கிறிஸ்தவர்களையும் கோதுமைப் பயிர்களான பரலோக நம்பிக்கையுள்ள கிறிஸ்தவர்களையும் பிரிக்கும் காலம், அதாவது அறுவடைக் காலம், 1914-ல் ஆரம்பித்தது என்று இப்போது நாம் சரியாகப் புரிந்திருக்கிறோம்.
Main source: The King Shines Light on the Kingdom

Title (English): Jehovah and Jesus inspect and refine the spiritual temple
Description (English): From 1914 to the early part of 1919, Jehovah and Jesus came to inspect the spiritual temple, as foretold at Malachi 3:1-4. Main source: “Who Really Is the Faithful and Discreet Slave?”

Title (English): The three and a half times (1,260 days) of Daniel 7 and 12
Description (English): During the three and a half times the anointed were harassed and “prophesied in sackcloth,” ending in mid-1918 when the Society’s leading members were convicted and imprisoned.
Description (Tamil): மூன்றரை காலங்கள் டிசம்பர் 1914 முதற்கொண்டு ஜூன் 1918 வரை
Main source: Identifying True Worshipers in the Time of the End

Title (English): Watch Tower begins to refine understanding of neutrality

Description (Tamil): செப்டம்பர் 1, 1915, காவற்கோபுரம் இன்னும் தெளிவான விளக்கம் கொடுத்தது.
Main source: Loyally Supporting God’s Government and No Other

Title (English): Russell departs on his final lecture tour
Description (English): Russell and his secretary Menta Sturgeon leave on a previously arranged lecture tour of the western and southwestern United States; his last talk is in Los Angeles on October 29.
Main source: A Time of Testing (1914-1918)

Title (English): C. T. Russell dies at age 64
Description (English): Charles Taze Russell dies on a train at Pampa, Texas, while traveling, at 64 years of age; his funeral is held in the New York City Temple on November 5.

Title (English): Watch Tower lists an editorial committee instead of one editor

Title (English): Newspaper sermon feature discontinued

Description (Tamil): என்று டிசம்பர் 15, 1916, காவற்கோபுரம் அறிவித்தது.
Main source: Methods of Preaching—Using Every Means to Reach People

Description (English): At the annual meeting, J. F. Rutherford becomes president of the Watch Tower Society, after an executive committee of three had administered affairs for about two months.

Title (English): J. F. Rutherford, second president of the Watch Tower Society
Description (English): Joseph F. Rutherford became president after Russell’s death and led the Bible Students, who took the name Jehovah’s Witnesses in 1931, until his death in San Diego.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Society begins assigning preaching territory
Description (English): The March 1, 1917, Watch Tower announces that all territory worked by colporteurs and congregation pastoral workers will be assigned by the Society’s office.
Main source: Development of the Organization Structure

Title (English): The Finished Mystery released to the Bethel family
Description (English): The Finished Mystery, the seventh volume of Studies in the Scriptures (a commentary on Revelation and Ezekiel), is released to the Bethel family at the dining table; by the end of 1917 an 850,000 edition is being printed.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Opposition from four directors; congregations split
Description (English): Four men serving on the Society’s board of directors become heated in their opposition when The Finished Mystery is released; Rutherford replaces them, and many congregations split after the summer of 1917.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Congregations encouraged to arrange juvenile Bible classes
Description (English): The Society encourages congregations to arrange a juvenile class for children aged 8 to 15.
Main source: Meetings for Worship, Instruction, and Encouragement

Title (English): Annual meeting confirms Rutherford’s leadership
Description (English): At the annual meeting the seven receiving the most votes are elected directors, with overwhelming support for J. F. Rutherford; opposers later splinter off, holding their own Memorial on March 26, 1918.
Main source: A Time of Testing (1914-1918)

Title (English): Canada bans The Finished Mystery
Description (English): Following a petition by some 600 Canadian clergymen, a government decree makes possession of The Finished Mystery or the tract Bible Students Monthly punishable by fine and imprisonment.
Main source: “Objects of Hatred by All the Nations”

Title (English): “The World Has Ended—Millions Now Living May Never Die” first delivered
Description (English): The discourse “The World Has Ended—Millions Now Living May Never Die” is first delivered, in Los Angeles, California.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Tract Kingdom News No. 1 released
Description (English): To expose clergy-inspired pressure against The Finished Mystery, the Society releases the tract Kingdom News No. 1; No. 2 follows on April 15 and No. 3 in May.
Main source: A Time of Testing (1914-1918)

Title (English): Boston talk titled “Millions Now Living Will Never Die”
Description (English): In Boston, Massachusetts, the talk is given under the title “The World Has Ended—Millions Now Living Will Never Die.”
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Federal arrest warrants issued for Rutherford and associates
Description (English): Clergy-inspired opposition culminates as U.S. federal warrants are issued for the arrest of J. F. Rutherford and close associates, charged under the Espionage Act.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Trial of the Society’s officers begins
Description (English): The trial of J. F. Rutherford and his associates begins.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Spanish influenza kills tens of millions
Description (English): The Spanish influenza, which invaded the battlefields of France in June 1918 and spread worldwide with returning troops, killed an estimated 20 million to 50 million people in 1918. The Watchtower presents it as a fulfillment of Jesus’ words “in one place after another pestilences” (Luke 21:11) and of the rider of the pale horse (Revelation 6:8).
Description (Tamil): “1918-⁠ல், ஸ்பானிஷ் ஃப்ளுவினால் 2 முதல் 5 கோடி பேர் உயிரிழந்தார்கள்; இப்படி உயிரிழந்தவர்களின் எண்ணிக்கை, பிளேக் நோயால் இறந்தவர்களைவிட அல்லது முதல் உலகப் போரில் இறந்தவர்களைவிட அதிகம்” என ஸுயெட்டாச்செ ட்ஸைட்டுங் என்ற செய்தித்தாள் அறிக்கை செய்கிறது.
Main source: Do You Recognize the Sign of Jesus’ Presence?
Notes: sort_key 1918.45 places it after the June 1918 outbreak in France (wp14 2/1 p. 5). Older publications speak of 1918-1919 (e.g. w91 4/1); the 2005 and 2014 articles cited here are used.

Title (English): Jury finds Rutherford and associates guilty
Description (English): A jury returns a verdict finding each of the defendants guilty on each count; principal members of the Society are convicted for material allegedly contrary to the war effort.
Main source: “Objects of Hatred by All the Nations”

Title (English): Rutherford and associates sentenced to long prison terms
Description (English): J. F. Rutherford and associates are sentenced to long terms (20 years for most) in federal penitentiary; one is sentenced on July 10. By mid-1918 eight are in the Atlanta penitentiary.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Imprisonment of J. F. Rutherford and his associates
Description (English): Convicted on false charges, Rutherford and seven associates were imprisoned in the federal penitentiary in Atlanta, Georgia, until they were released on bail in March 1919; the conviction was later reversed.
People: Joseph F. Rutherford; W. E. Van Amburgh; A. H. Macmillan; R. J. Martin; F. H. Robison; C. J. Woodworth; G. H. Fisher; G. DeCecca
Main source: Dates (Calendar)

Title (English): Brooklyn headquarters closed; operations moved to Pittsburgh
Description (English): With the officers imprisoned and coal unavailable, the Brooklyn headquarters is closed and operations transferred back to Pittsburgh (119 Federal Street) for over a year.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses
Start/end of span: start of Headquarters operations moved back to Pittsburgh (b12-0074)

Title (English): Headquarters operations moved back to Pittsburgh
Description (English): While Rutherford and his associates were imprisoned, the Brooklyn headquarters was closed and its operations were transferred back to Pittsburgh for over a year.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Babylon the Great evidently fallen
Title (Tamil): 1919-ல் மகா பாபிலோன் வீழ்ந்துவிட்டது என்பது தெளிவாகத் தெரிந்தது
Description (English): As the angels’ collecting of the weedlike Christians progressed after 1914, the distinction between true and imitation Christians became ever clearer. By 1919 it became evident that Babylon the Great had fallen.
Description (Tamil): களைகளைப் பிடுங்கப் பிடுங்க, இரண்டு வகுப்பாருக்கும் இடையிலுள்ள வித்தியாசம் பளிச்சென தெரிய ஆரம்பித்தது. (வெளி. 18:1, 4) 1919-ல் மகா பாபிலோன் வீழ்ந்துவிட்டது என்பது தெளிவாகத் தெரிந்தது.
Main source: “Look! I Am With You All the Days”
Notes: English: 'By 1919' (precision 'before'); the Tamil edition says '1919-ல்' (in 1919).

Title (English): The Bulletin published to stimulate field service
Description (English): The Bulletin (forerunner of Our Kingdom Ministry, later called Director and Informant) begins publication as a stimulus to field service.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Service director appointed in each congregation
Description (English): In each congregation a service director is appointed theocratically by the branch office to organize field service, and field service begins to be reported weekly.
Description (Tamil): ஒவ்வொரு சபையிலும் ஊழிய வேலையை ஒழுங்கமைக்கவும் ஊழியத்தில் கலந்துகொள்ளும்படி சபையாரை உற்சாகப்படுத்தவும் சர்வீஸ் டைரக்டரை கிளை அலுவலகம் நியமித்தது. இந்த ஏற்பாட்டை சில மூப்பர்கள் ஆதரிக்கவில்லை.
Main source: Organized to Serve “the God of Peace”

Title (English): 1919 report: 5,793 preaching in 43 lands
Description (English): The report for the year shows 5,793 Bible Students actively preaching in 43 lands, with Memorial attendance of 21,411.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Rutherford reelected while in prison
Description (English): At the annual meeting held with a convention in Pittsburgh (January 2-5, 1919), J. F. Rutherford is reelected president while imprisoned.
Main source: Advertise the King and the Kingdom! (1919-1941)

Title (English): League of Nations officially proposed; the 1,290 days begin
Description (English): The League of Nations, the first form of “the disgusting thing that is causing desolation,” was officially proposed in January 1919. With this, both conditions of Daniel 12:11 were met, so the 1,290 days began in early 1919.
Description (Tamil): ஜனவரி 1919-ல், சர்வதேச சங்கம் அதிகாரப்பூர்வமாய் முன்மொழியப்பட்டது.
Main source: Identifying True Worshipers in the Time of the End

Title (English): The 1,290 days of Daniel 12:11
Description (English): The 1,290 days began in early 1919, when the League of Nations was proposed, and ran until the autumn of 1922; during them the anointed awakened and progressed spiritually.
Description (Tamil): ஆகவே 1,290 நாட்கள், 1919-ன் ஆரம்பத்தில் துவங்கி, 1922-ன் (வட அரைகோள) இலையுதிர்காலம் வரை நீடித்தன.
Main source: Identifying True Worshipers in the Time of the End

Title (English): Faithful Bible Students revived after the 1918 test
Description (English): After the 1918 imprisonment of J. F. Rutherford and seven associates made the work seem paralyzed and the clergy thought the Bible Students 'dead,' God's spirit revived the faithful ones from early in 1919, fulfilling Revelation 11:11.
Description (Tamil): எது நடக்கவே நடக்காது என்று எதிரிகள் நினைத்தார்களோ அது 1919-ல் நடக்க ஆரம்பித்தது; கடவுளுடைய சக்தியினால் உண்மையுள்ளவர்கள் புத்துயிர் பெற்றார்கள்!
Main source: The Kingdom Is Born in Heaven

Title (English): Christ appoints the faithful and discreet slave over his domestics
Description (English): In 1919, a time of spiritual revival, Jesus selected capable anointed brothers from among the refined Bible Students to be 'the faithful and discreet slave,' appointing them over his domestics to provide spiritual food at the proper time.
Description (Tamil): 1919-ல், அவர்களிலிருந்து தகுதியுள்ள பரலோக நம்பிக்கையுள்ள சகோதரர்களை இயேசு உண்மையும் விவேகமும் உள்ள அடிமையாகத் தேர்ந்தெடுத்து தம் வீட்டார் மீது நியமித்தார்.
Main source: “Who Really Is the Faithful and Discreet Slave?”
Where sources differ: w13 7/15 par. 3 records the earlier understanding (slave appointed over domestics at Pentecost 33 C.E., over 'all his belongings' in 1919) and clarifies it: appointment over domestics in 1919; appointment over all belongings still future, at Christ's coming during the great tribulation.

Title (English): Society’s officers released on bail
Description (English): Rutherford and his associates are released from prison on bail in Brooklyn, the appeals court having ordered bail on March 21.
Description (Tamil): சகோதரர் ரதர்ஃபர்டும் மற்ற சகோதரர்களும் மார்ச் 26, 1919-ல் சிறையிலிருந்து விடுதலை செய்யப்பட்டார்கள்.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses
Start/end of span: end of Imprisonment of J. F. Rutherford and his associates (b12-0073)

Title (English): Public lecture “The Hope for Distressed Humanity” in Los Angeles
Description (English): As a test of whether the work can be revived, Rutherford gives the lecture “The Hope for Distressed Humanity” at Clune’s Auditorium, Los Angeles; the crowd cannot all fit in and it is repeated.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Court of appeals reverses the convictions
Description (English): The U.S. court of appeals reverses the lower court’s decision against the Society’s officers and orders a new trial.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Pamphlet To Whom the Work Is Entrusted urges house-to-house preaching
Title (Tamil): யாரிடம் இந்த வேலை ஒப்படைக்கப்பட்டிருக்கிறது (ஆங்கிலம்) என்ற கைப்பிரதி
Description (English): The pamphlet To Whom the Work Is Entrusted, published in 1919, urged all anointed Christians to preach from house to house. The preaching work especially set true Christians apart from imitation ones, and house-to-house preaching became their hallmark.
Description (Tamil): உதாரணத்திற்கு, 1919-ல் பிரசுரிக்கப்பட்ட யாரிடம் இந்த வேலை ஒப்படைக்கப்பட்டிருக்கிறது (ஆங்கிலம்) என்ற கைப்பிரதி பரலோக நம்பிக்கையுள்ள கிறிஸ்தவர்கள் எல்லோரையும் வீட்டுக்கு வீடு ஊழியத்தில் ஈடுபட உந்துவித்தது.
Main source: “Look! I Am With You All the Days”
Notes: The article adds that The Watch Tower reported in 1922 that the Bible Students had stepped up their preaching from that time onward.

Title (English): Wheat gathered into the storehouse: anointed gathered into the restored congregation
Title (Tamil): 1919 முதற்கொண்டு பரலோக நம்பிக்கையுள்ள கிறிஸ்தவர்கள் சுத்திகரிக்கப்பட்ட கிறிஸ்தவ சபைக்குள் கூட்டிச் சேர்க்கப்படுகிறார்கள்
Description (English): Jesus commands his angels: “Go to gathering the wheat into my storehouse.” Since 1919, anointed ones have been gathered into the restored Christian congregation; for those alive at the end of this system, the final gathering will take place when they receive their heavenly reward.
Description (Tamil): இரண்டாவது, கோதுமையைச் சேர்ப்பது. “கோதுமையை என்னுடைய களஞ்சியத்தில் சேர்த்து வையுங்கள்” என்று தேவதூதர்களுக்கு இயேசு கட்டளையிடுகிறார். (மத். 13:30) 1919 முதற்கொண்டு பரலோக நம்பிக்கையுள்ள கிறிஸ்தவர்கள் சுத்திகரிக்கப்பட்ட கிறிஸ்தவ சபைக்குள் கூட்டிச் சேர்க்கப்படுகிறார்கள்.
Main source: “Look! I Am With You All the Days”
Notes: Ongoing; the article places the final gathering in the future, when the anointed alive at the end receive their heavenly reward (b10-0016).

Title (English): Cedar Point convention; The Golden Age announced
Title (Tamil): த கோல்டன் ஏஜ் (இப்போது விழித்தெழு! என்று அழைக்கப்படுகிறது) பத்திரிகை பிரசுரிக்கப்படும் என்று அறிவிக்கப்பட்டது.
Description (English): Bible Students gather at Cedar Point, Ohio, for their first major convention after World War I; the preaching work is revitalized and the coming magazine The Golden Age (now Awake!) is announced.

Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Headquarters activity resumes in Brooklyn
Description (English): By the first of October 1919 the headquarters staff is once again carrying on its activity from Brooklyn.
Main source: Producing Bible Literature for Use in the Ministry
Start/end of span: end of Headquarters operations moved back to Pittsburgh (b12-0074)

Title (English): First issue of The Golden Age
Description (English): The magazine The Golden Age (later Consolation, now Awake!), designed to appeal to the public, is released with its first issue dated October 1, 1919.

Title (English): The Golden Age magazine
Description (English): The Golden Age, a magazine for the general public, was first released on October 1, 1919; in 1937 it was renamed Consolation.

Title (English): Bulletin / Our Kingdom Ministry (monthly service publication)
Description (English): The Bulletin, first published in 1919 to stimulate field service, later became Our Kingdom Ministry; in 2015 it was announced that it would be replaced by the Our Christian Life and Ministry—Meeting Workbook.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses
Notes: End = announcement of October 3, 2015; the first Meeting Workbook issue is dated January 2016.

Title (English): Watch Tower Society begins its own printing in Brooklyn
Description (English): The Society undertakes its own printing operations in rented factory space in Brooklyn (35 Myrtle Avenue), beginning with magazines.
Description (Tamil): பின்னர் 1920-ல், வாடகைக்கு எடுக்கப்பட்ட தொழிற்சாலைகளில் சில பிரசுரங்களை யெகோவாவின் சாட்சிகள் தயாரித்தனர்.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Booklet Millions Now Living Will Never Die points to 1925
Description (English): The booklet Millions Now Living Will Never Die expresses the expectation that 1925 would mark the return of faithful men of old; the year came and went without that occurring.
Main source: Advertise the King and the Kingdom! (1919-1941)

Title (English): League of Nations comes into existence (“the wild beast . . . was”)
Description (English): The League of Nations, promoted by Britain and the United States, existed from January 10, 1920, onward, with 63 nations participating at one time or another. Jehovah’s Witnesses identify it as the image of the wild beast of Revelation 13 and the scarlet-colored wild beast of Revelation 17.
Description (Tamil): ஆம், 63 தேசங்கள் ஒரு சமயத்திலோ அல்லது வேறொரு சமயத்திலோ பங்கெடுத்தன; ஜனவரி 10, 1920 முதல் சர்வதேச சங்கமாக அது இருந்தது.
Main source: An Awesome Mystery Solved
Start/end of span: start of The League of Nations (the image of the wild beast) (b14-0007)

Title (English): The League of Nations (the image of the wild beast)
Description (English): The League of Nations “was” from 1920 until the start of World War II. When the Nazi dictator of Germany launched the war in September 1939, the League, having failed to keep peace, virtually plunged into an abyss of inactivity (“is not”).
Description (Tamil): 1920-ல், சர்வதேச சங்கம் ஏற்படுத்தப்படுகிறது. இரண்டாம் உலகப் போர் ஆரம்பிக்கும்வரை அது செயல்படுகிறது.
Main source: An Awesome Mystery Solved
Notes: End taken as the start of World War II (September 1939), when, per re ch. 34, the League “virtually plunged into an abyss of inactivity”; by 1942 it had become “a has-been.”

Title (English): Government withdraws the case against the Society’s officers
Description (English): After the defendants appear in court five times, the government’s attorney announces in open court in Brooklyn the withdrawal of the prosecution.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Watch Tower article “Gospel of the Kingdom”
Description (English): The July 1, 1920, Watch Tower article “Gospel of the Kingdom” shows that now is the time to proclaim the good news of the end of the old order and the establishment of Messiah’s Kingdom.
Description (Tamil): ஜூலை 1, 1920, காவற்கோபுரத்தில் “கடவுளுடைய அரசாங்கத்தைப் பற்றிய நல்ல செய்தி”
Main source: People Who Preach—Ministers Offer Themselves Willingly

Title (English): Over two million Russians starve to death
Description (English): The Watchtower lists the famine of 1921, in which over two million Russians starved to death, among the famines of the 20th century that it connects with the rider of the black horse (Revelation 6:5, 6) and Jesus’ words about food shortages.
Main source: The True Culprit Behind War and Suffering

Title (English): The Harp of God published
Description (English): The Bible study aid The Harp of God is published.
Main source: Tools for Preaching—Producing Literature for the Worldwide Field

Title (English): Convention resolution “A Challenge to World Leaders”
Description (English): The 1922 convention adopts the resolution “A Challenge to World Leaders,” first of seven yearly resolutions (1922-1928) distributed widely.
Main source: Conventions Proof of Our Brotherhood

Title (English): Clergy in Germany agitate for arrests of Bible Students
Description (English): Clergy in Germany agitate for police to arrest Bible Students engaged in public distribution of Bible literature.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Watch Tower points to two organizations, Jehovah’s and Satan’s
Description (English): The Watch Tower points out that there are two organizations at work, Jehovah’s and Satan’s, Satan’s being made up of commercial, religious, and political elements.
Description (Tamil): இது சம்பந்தமாக 1922-ல் வெளிவந்த காவற்கோபுரம், இரண்டு அமைப்புகள் இருப்பதாகச் சொன்னது.
Main source: The King Shines Light on the Kingdom
Where sources differ: jv events table attributes the explanation of two opposing organizations to the March 1, 1925, Watch Tower; kr ch. 5 says the point was made in 1922 (kr is newer).

Title (English): Small printing plant set up in Korea
Description (English): The Society sets up a small printing plant in Korea able to produce literature in Korean, Japanese, and Chinese.
Main source: Producing Bible Literature for Use in the Ministry

Title (English): Rutherford’s first radio broadcast
Description (English): Radio is used for the first time as J. F. Rutherford broadcasts a Bible discourse in California.
Description (Tamil): ரேடியோ
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Printing moves to 18 Concord Street, Brooklyn
Description (English): The Society moves its printing into a leased six-story building at 18 Concord Street, Brooklyn, where it begins printing and binding books.
Main source: Producing Bible Literature for Use in the Ministry

Title (English): Broadcast from Metropolitan Opera House, Philadelphia
Description (English): Rutherford gives a historic radio broadcast of “Millions Now Living Will Never Die” from the Metropolitan Opera House in Philadelphia, heard by an estimated 50,000.
Description (Tamil): ஏப்ரல் 16, 1922-ல் பென்ஸில்வேனியாவைச் சேர்ந்த பிலடெல்ஃபியாவிலுள்ள மெட்ரோபாலிட்டன் ஓப்ரா ஹவுஸிலிருந்து சகோதரர் ரதர்ஃபர்ட்டின் பேச்சு ஒலிபரப்பப்பட்டது.
Main source: Methods of Preaching—Using Every Means to Reach People

Title (English): Study questions become a regular Watch Tower feature
Description (English): Following a recommendation by pilgrims that a regular meeting study The Watch Tower, questions for studying principal articles become a regular feature beginning with the May 15, 1922, issue.
Description (Tamil): சபைகளில் பேச்சுகளைக் கொடுப்பதற்கும் பிரசங்க வேலையை முன்நின்று வழிநடத்துவதற்கும் காவற்கோபுர சங்கத்தால் அனுப்பிவைக்கப்பட்ட ஊழியர்கள் 1922-ல் ஒரு விஷயத்தைச் சிபாரிசு செய்தார்கள்.
Main source: Meetings for Worship, Instruction, and Encouragement

Title (English): Cedar Point convention: “Advertise, advertise, advertise”
Description (English): At the nine-day Cedar Point, Ohio, convention, Rutherford’s talk “The Kingdom” urges: “Advertise, advertise, advertise, the King and his kingdom,” giving great impetus to the preaching work.
Description (Tamil): “கடவுளுடைய அரசாங்கம்” என்ற தலைப்பில் கொடுக்கப்பட்ட பேச்சு, பிரசங்க வேலையைச் செய்ய எல்லாரையும் உற்சாகப்படுத்தியது. இந்தப் பேச்சில்தான், “ராஜாவையும் அவருடைய அரசாங்கத்தையும் விளம்பரப்படுத்துங்கள், விளம்பரப்படுத்துங்கள், விளம்பரப்படுத்துங்கள்” என்ற அறிவிப்பு செய்யப்பட்டது.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): The 1,335 days of Daniel 12:12
Description (English): The 1,335 days ran from the Cedar Point convention of September 1922 to May 1926, when the anointed attained a happy state with a clear focus on the sanctification of Jehovah’s name.
Description (Tamil): முன்னறிவிக்கப்பட்டபடி, 1,335 நாட்களின் முடிவில் பரிசுத்தவான்கள் சந்தோஷமான நிலையில் இருந்தார்கள்.
Main source: Identifying True Worshipers in the Time of the End

Title (English): Watch Tower draws attention to a class with earthly hope
Description (English): The Watch Tower draws attention to a group with no heavenly aspirations who would live on earth under Christ’s reign, connected with the parable of the sheep and the goats.
Main source: The King Shines Light on the Kingdom

Title (English): First broadcast of a convention session
Description (English): A convention session is broadcast by radio for the first time.
Description (Tamil): பிறகு, 1923-ல் முதன்முதலாக ஒரு மாநாட்டின் ஒரு பாகம் ஒலிபரப்பப்பட்டது.
Main source: Methods of Preaching—Using Every Means to Reach People

Title (English): Monthly field-service testimonies (forerunner of Service Meeting)
Description (English): For much of 1923, a monthly meeting focused on field service is held, with half of the Wednesday-night meeting given to field-service testimonies.
Description (Tamil): 1923-லிருந்து மாதத்துக்கு ஒருமுறை ஊழியக் கூட்டம் நடத்தப்பட்டது.
Main source: Meeting Together for Worship

Title (English): Nathan H. Knorr baptized
Description (English): Eighteen-year-old Nathan H. Knorr is baptized in the Little Lehigh River, Pennsylvania; on September 6, 1923, he becomes a member of the Bethel family.
Main source: Declaring the Good News Without Letup (1942-1975)

Title (English): Resolution “Ecclesiastics Indicted” distributed
Description (English): The 1924 convention resolution “Ecclesiastics Indicted” is distributed by Bible Students in many lands during 1924-25.
Main source: Conventions Proof of Our Brotherhood

Title (English): WBBR, the Society’s own radio station, begins broadcasting
Description (English): WBBR on Staten Island, New York, the first radio station owned by the Watch Tower Society, makes its first broadcast; by 1926 the Bible Students own six stations.
Description (Tamil): பிப்ரவரி 24, 1924-ல் அந்தப் புதிய வானொலி நிலையத்திலிருந்து முதல் ஒலிபரப்பு செய்யப்பட்டது.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses
Start/end of span: start of Radio station WBBR operated by the Watch Tower Society (b12-0079)

Title (English): Radio station WBBR operated by the Watch Tower Society
Description (English): WBBR, the first radio station owned by the Watch Tower Society, broadcast Bible discourses from Staten Island, New York, from 1924 until it was sold in 1957.

Main source: I Have Benefited From Walking With Wise Ones

Title (English): Songbook Kingdom Hymns published
Description (English): The songbook Kingdom Hymns is published.
Main source: Meeting Together for Worship

Title (English): Watch Tower article “Birth of the Nation”
Description (English): The March 1, 1925, Watch Tower article “Birth of the Nation” shows that the Messianic Kingdom was born in heaven in 1914, fulfilling Revelation chapter 12, and that Satan was then hurled down.

Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Watch Tower article “Who Will Honor Jehovah?”
Description (English): The principal article of the January 1, 1926, Watch Tower presents the issue each individual must face, “Who Will Honor Jehovah?”, highlighting the meaning of God’s name.
Description (Tamil): அதனால்தான், ஜனவரி 1, 1926, காவற்கோபுரம் இப்படிச் சொன்னது: “யெகோவா என்ற பெயர், .
Main source: How We Came to Be Known as Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): House-to-house preaching with books on Sunday encouraged
Description (English): House-to-house preaching with books on Sundays is encouraged; during 1927 publishers are urged to spend part of every Sunday in group witnessing.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Bible Students own six radio stations
Description (English): By 1926 the Bible Students own six radio stations: WBBR in New York, WORD near Chicago, and four in Canada.
Description (Tamil): யெகோவாவின் மக்கள் 1926-க்குள் சொந்தமாக ஆறு வானொலி நிலையங்களை அமைத்தார்கள்.
Main source: Methods of Preaching—Using Every Means to Reach People

Title (English): Pilgrims become supervisors of field service
Description (English): Rutherford begins changing the work of pilgrims from traveling speakers into traveling supervisors and promoters of congregation field service; in 1928 they are called regional service directors.
Main source: Development of the Organization Structure

Title (English): Legal department established at Magdeburg, Germany
Description (English): With 897 cases pending in German courts, the Watch Tower Society establishes a legal department at its Magdeburg branch.
Main source: ‘Defending and Legally Establishing the Good News’

Title (English): Convention in May 1926; book Deliverance released; the 1,335 days end
Title (Tamil): மே 1926-ல் நடந்த மாநாட்டில் விடுதலை என்ற ஆங்கில புத்தகம் வெளியிடப்பட்டது.
Description (English): At the convention in May 1926, the book Deliverance was released, one of a series of new books to replace Studies in the Scriptures. Daniel’s Prophecy explains that the 1,335 days of Daniel 12:12 thus ended with the holy ones in a happy state.
Description (Tamil): மே 1926-ல் நடந்த மாநாட்டில் விடுதலை என்ற ஆங்கில புத்தகம் வெளியிடப்பட்டது.
Main source: Identifying True Worshipers in the Time of the End

Title (English): Society prints The Emphatic Diaglott on its own presses
Description (English): In December 1926 the Society prints The Emphatic Diaglott, Benjamin Wilson’s translation of the Christian Greek Scriptures, on a flatbed press at its Concord Street factory.
Description (Tamil): அதற்காக, 1926-ல் த எம்ஃபடிக் டயக்லாட், அதாவது பென்ஜமின் வில்சன் மொழிபெயர்த்த கிறிஸ்தவ கிரேக்க வேதாகமம், நம் சொந்த அச்சகத்தில் அச்சடிக்கப்பட்டது.
Main source: Tools for Preaching—Producing Literature for the Worldwide Field

Title (English): Last Christmas celebrated at Brooklyn Bethel
Description (English): The Bethel family in Brooklyn celebrates Christmas for the last time; after 1926 Christmas begins to be recognized as pagan in origin.
Main source: The King Refines His People Spiritually
Notes: Day not given in source; 1926 is the year.

Title (English): Society moves into its own factory at 117 Adams Street, Brooklyn
Description (English): The Society moves into its newly constructed eight-story factory building at 117 Adams Street, Brooklyn, from which much more literature is produced.
Description (Tamil): ஆனால் 1927 முதல், உவாட்ச் டவர் பைபிள் அண்டு டிராக்ட் சொஸைட்டி ஆஃப் நியூ யார்க்கிற்கு சொந்தமான எட்டு மாடி தொழிற்சாலை கட்டடத்தில் அதிகமான பிரசுரங்கள் தயாரிக்கப்பட்டன.
Main source: Producing Bible Literature for Use in the Ministry

Title (English): Faithful and wise servant reaffirmed as collective
Description (English): The Watch Tower of February 15, 1927, reaffirms that the faithful and wise servant is a collective servant, not one individual.
Main source: Growing in Accurate Knowledge of the Truth

Title (English): Toronto convention talk carried by unparalleled radio network
Description (English): Rutherford’s lecture “Freedom for the Peoples” to some 15,000 at Toronto, Canada, is heard by millions through a hitherto unparalleled radio network.
Main source: Part 2—United States of America

Title (English): Swiss Federal Supreme Court rules confiscating tracts violates freedom of belief
Description (English): In the case of Adolf Huber, Switzerland’s Federal Supreme Court finds that confiscating religious tracts violates “freedom of belief,” stopping police interference with the Bible Students’ ministry.
Description (Tamil): தீர்ப்பு அந்த போலீஸ் அதிகாரியின் செயல் தவறு என்று உச்ச நீதிமன்றத்தில் சகோதரர் ஹூபர் சொன்னார். மதம் சம்பந்தப்பட்ட துண்டுப்பிரதிகளைப் பறிமுதல் செய்வது ஒருவரின் “மதச் சுதந்திரத்துக்கு” எதிரானது என்று நீதிமன்றம் தீர்ப்பளித்தது.
Main source: Kingdom Preachers Take Their Case to Court

Title (English): The Golden Age notes Christmas is a pagan celebration
Description (English): The Golden Age of December 14, 1927, notes that Christmas is a pagan celebration that focuses on pleasures and involves idol worship.
Main source: The King Refines His People Spiritually

Title (English): Bible Students arrested in New Jersey for house-to-house preaching
Description (English): Bible Students are arrested in South Amboy, New Jersey, for distributing literature from house to house; within a decade such arrests exceed 500 a year in the United States.
Main source: Noteworthy Events in the Modern-day History of Jehovah’s Witnesses

Title (English): Cross-and-crown emblems shown to be objectionable (Detroit)
Description (English): At the 1928 assembly in Detroit, Michigan, cross-and-crown emblems are shown to be not only unnecessary but objectionable.
Description (Tamil): 1928-ல் அமெரிக்காவில், மிச்சிகனிலுள்ள டெட்ராய்ட் என்ற இடத்தில் நடந்த மாநாட்டில் சொல்லப்பட்ட விஷயத்தைப் பற்றி சகோதரர் க்ரான்ட் சூட்டர் (இவர் பிற்பாடு, ஆளும் குழு அங்கத்தினராகச் சேவை செய்தவர்) இப்படிச் சொன்னார்: “சிலுவையும் கிரீடமும் கொண்ட சின்னங்களைப் பயன்படுத்த வேண்டியதில்லை என்று சொல்லப்பட்டதோடு அதைப் பயன்படுத்துவது தவறு என்றும் அந்த மாநாட்டில் சொல்லப்பட்டது.”
Main source: The King Refines His People Spiritually

Title (English): Watch Tower stresses the Kingdom above personal salvation
Description (English): The Watch Tower begins to stress that the Kingdom is more important than personal salvation by means of the ransom.
Description (Tamil): மீட்புவிலை மூலம் நமக்குக் கிடைக்கும் மீட்பைவிட கடவுளுடைய அரசாங்கம்தான் மிக முக்கியம் என்பதை 1928-ல் வெளிவந்த காவற்கோபுர கட்டுரைகள் வலியுறுத்த ஆரம்பித்தன.
Main source: The King Shines Light on the Kingdom

Title (English): Songbook Songs of Praise to Jehovah published
Description (English): The songbook Songs of Praise to Jehovah is published.
Main source: Meeting Together for Worship

Title (English): Bible Students’ radio stations in Canada lose licenses
Description (English): Under clergy pressure, all the stations in Canada run by the Bible Students lose their licenses; lectures continue on commercial stations.
Main source: Methods of Preaching—Using Every Means to Reach People

Title (English): Congregations urged to hold Service Meeting weekly
Description (English): By 1928 congregations are urged to hold a meeting for field service each week.
Main source: Meeting Together for Worship

Title (English): Exposé “Christmas, Its Origin and Purpose”
Description (English): A thorough exposé of Christmas by Richard H. Barber is published in The Golden Age of December 12, 1928, as “Christmas, Its Origin and Purpose.”

Main source: The King Refines His People Spiritually

Title (English): Book Prophecy: Jehovah’s name the vital issue
Description (English): The book Prophecy states that “Jehovah’s name is the most vital issue before all creation.”
Main source: Jehovah Exalts His Name

Title (English): Superior authorities explained as Jehovah and Jesus
Description (English): Beginning in 1929, publications reason that the “superior authorities” of Romans 13:1 are not secular rulers but Jehovah and Jesus (a view later refined).
Description (Tamil): ‘அதிகாரத்தில் இருக்கிறவர்கள்’ என ரோமர் 13:1 -ல் சொல்லப்பட்டுள்ள வார்த்தைகள், உலக அதிகாரிகளை அர்த்தப்படுத்தவில்லை, யெகோவாவையும் இயேசுவையும்தான் அர்த்தப்படுத்துகிறது என 1929-ன் ஆரம்பத்தில் வெளிவந்த நம் பிரசுரங்கள் விளக்கின.
Main source: The King Shines Light on the Kingdom

Title (English): Two-volume Light on Revelation published
Description (English): A study of Revelation reflecting developments since 1917 is published in the two volumes entitled Light.
Main source: Growing in Accurate Knowledge of the Truth

Title (English): German Interior Ministry halts peddling prosecutions
Description (English): After thousands of cases, Germany’s Ministry of the Interior issues a circular telling police to stop initiating legal action against Bible Students under peddling laws.
Main source: “Objects of Hatred by All the Nations”

Title (English): Vindication, Book 1, published
Description (English): The first of the three-volume commentary Vindication is published.
Main source: The Great Crowd to Live in Heaven? Or on Earth?

Title (English): Columbus, Ohio, convention broadcast over vast radio network
Description (English): Some 15,000 Bible Students meet at Columbus, Ohio, July 24-30; part of the program is transmitted over what was then the most extensive radio chain broadcast ever aired.
Description (Tamil): ஜூலை 1931-ல், அமெரிக்கா, ஒஹாயோவிலுள்ள கொலம்பஸில் நடந்த மாநாட்டுக்குச் சுமார் 15,000 பைபிள் மாணாக்கர்கள் வந்திருந்தார்கள்.
